DM IZAL BRIEF REMARKS FOR THE EVENT TO MARK THE
COMPLETION OF MAQAM HABIB NOH REJUVENATION WORKS
ON SUNDAY, 11 JANUARY 2026

Acting Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs,
Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim,

Member of Parliament for Jalan Besar GRC,
Dr. Wan Rizal,

President of MUIS, Mr Mohammed Sa’at Abdul Rahman

Chief Executive of MUIS, Mr Kadir Maideen,

Deputy Chief Executive, Mr Azree Rahim

Senior Director of One Mosque Sector, Mr Zalman Ali,

The Chairman and Respected Members of Haji Muhammad Salleh Mosque Management Board,

Distinguished guests,

Assalāmu‘alaikum warahmatullāhi wabarakātuh.

1. As I look around at the faces gathered here, I am reminded that what we celebrate today transcends the mere restoration of a sacred site. Rather, it is a timely reflection on the life of Habib Sayyid Noh bin Sayyid Mohamad bin Sayyid Ahmad Al-Habshi, and our way of honouring him through our collective dedication to preserving not just his resting place, but to try and embody the values he championed throughout his life.

The Life of Service 

2. Throughout Malaya, Habib Nuh travelled, not as a distant scholar preaching from the mimbar, but as a compassionate teacher who walked among the people. His dakwah was lived, not merely spoken. Every interaction became an opportunity to demonstrate Islamic values – whether he was comforting a grieving family, teaching children the Quran, or simply sharing a meal with the poor.

Dakwah Through Compassion

3. What made Habib Nuh's dakwah so effective was his understanding that Islam's beauty is best revealed through acts of mercy and kindness. He was renowned for his boundless compassion, particularly towards children and orphans, whom he would delight with sweets and small gifts. But these gestures were never mere charity – they were dakwah in action, showing the community that Islam teaches us to care for the most vulnerable among us.

4. On his regular counsel and guidance to the community, people would seek him out not just for religious instruction, but for his wisdom in resolving disputes, his comfort in times of sorrow, and his guidance in matters both spiritual and worldly. Through these interactions, he demonstrated that Islam is not confined to the mosque, but is a complete way of life that addresses every human need.

Dakwah Through Unity, Never Division

5. Habib Nuh's dakwah was characterised by its unifying nature. In an era when communities often faced external pressures and internal disagreements, he chose the path of reconciliation and understanding. His approach to dakwah was never divisive, even during the most challenging and turbulent times.

6. This inclusive approach to dakwah made him beloved across all segments of society. Shopkeepers welcomed his presence. The community embraced his teachings because they saw in him a living example of Islamic principles – generosity, humility, compassion, and justice.

7. Among his most treasured words were these: "Do not be greedy for worldly materials, nor harbour ill-feelings towards anyone throughout your life."
Reflections on Mortality and Purpose

8. The passing of such a righteous soul reminds us of fundamental truths about our existence. As believers, we understand that death is not an end but an awakening to a different realm of existence. Saidina Ali (r.a.) once said: when people pass away, they truly wake up to reality.

9. This awareness of mortality is infact wisdom. It focuses our attention on what truly matters in this fleeting life.

10. The great scholar Sahl ibn Abdillah was once asked when we can truly rest from one’s ego. His reply was: When an individual understands that he possesses only the present moment in which he exists.

11. Allah tells us in the Quran: "Verily, the awliya’ of Allah shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve."

12. They have no fear because they are certain of their present state and trust completely in Allah's plan for them.

13. Ibn Ata'illah As-Sakandari captured this beautifully when he said: "The heedless person wakes up in the morning asking, 'What shall I do today?' But the wise person asks, 'What will Allah do with me today?'"
ا ل إذا أ ظر ذا ل ، وا ل ظر ذا ل هل هّل . 14 ا ا يهنملقفغعصحبا

15. In Habib Nuh, we see the living embodiment of this wisdom – a man who never asked "What can I achieve today?" but rather "How can I serve Allah's purpose today?" This mindset shaped every aspect of his dakwah and community service.
Conclusion

16. As we honour Habib Nuh today through the completion of this restoration, we must remember that the greatest tribute we can pay to his memory is to continue his mission of dakwah. Not through grand gestures or speeches alone, but through the same gentle, inclusive, and unifying approach that made his dakwah so effective. May his legacy continue to inspire us towards righteousness and service to others.

17. Rabbana aslih lana dinana alladhi huwa 'ismatu amrina, wa aslih lana dunyaana allati fiha ma'ashuna, wa aslih lana akhiratana allati ilayha ma'aduna.

18. Our Lord, make righteous for us our religion which is the safeguard of our affairs, make righteous for us our worldly life in which is our livelihood, and make righteous for us our Hereafter to which is our return.

Opening Remarks

It is an honour to be here today to mark the completion of Maqam Habib Noh rejuvenation works. But beyond that, today is also a celebration of our community’s unity and dedication.

Gratitude to Generous Donors

2 I want to thank all the donors and sponsors of this project. Your generosity shows the importance of preserving our Islamic heritage. With your contributions, Maqam Habib Noh will continue to inspire faith for many more generations to come. May Allah reward you an abundance of blessings for your contributions.
Recognition of Exemplary Leadership

3 To the MUIS team, Chairman and the Mosque Management Board of Masjid Haji Muhammad Salleh, I commend your unwavering dedication throughout this extensive project. From the initial planning stages to today’s completion, you have demonstrated exceptional stewardship and commitment to serving the community. This exemplifies true service to both community and Islamic heritage.

Community Unity and Support

4 I also want to extend my heartfelt gratitude to our wider Muslim community. Your patience, prayers, and continuous support during the closure reflect the true spirit of our ummah. This project’s success is a shared achievement that belongs to all of us.
Future Aspirations

5 Looking ahead, I pray that Maqam Habib Noh will remain a "Spiritual Oasis in the City." May it continue to be a place of peace, barakah, and inspiration for visitors from Singapore and beyond. The upcoming publication of a book on its history will further strengthen our understanding and appreciation of this unique heritage.

6 May Allah SWT accept our collective efforts throughout this rejuvenation project.

11 Semoga Maqam Habib Noh akan terus berkembang sebagai "Spiritual Oasis in the City" atau “Oasis Kerohanian di Tengah Bandar” sewajar dengan ukiran sejarah melebihi satu abad.

12 Terima kasih kepada MUIS, Lembaga Pentadbir Masjid, para penderma yang dermawan, kakitangan dan sukarelawan atas usaha anda. Semoga Allah SWT menerima usaha kolektif kita dalam menjayakan projek pemuliharaan ini.

Qaadku sida la sheego waa maandooriye caafimaadka qofka cuna iyo noloshiisaba halis ku ah. In badan oo inaga mid ah oo aan ka mid ahaa waxa ay is weydiiyaan sababta geedkan caafimaadka iyo noloshaba halista ku ah ay dawladdu u joojin wayday iyo waxa ay dhawranayso ee ka hortaagan in ay falkan ku dhaqaaqdo. 

Qaadku waa badeecad badankeedu inooga timaaddo waddanka dibaddiisa ama waddamada jaarka—Itoobiya iyo Kenya badanka. Marka uu waddanka soo gelayo waxa uu soo maraa kastamo, halkaas oo cashuur lagaga qaado. Cashuurtaas laga qaadaa waxa ay ka mid tahay dakhliga dawladda soo gala ee ay dawladdu ku tiirsan tahay, miisaaniyaddana qayb weyn buu ka yahay. Qaadka waxa kale oo ku tiirsan dadka ka ganacsada iyo kuwa ka shaqeeya oo uu u yahay il dhaqaale kasoo galo. Sidoo kale, qaadka waxa si aan toos ahayn ugu tiirsan maqaaxiyaha lagu qayilo, dadka leh boosaska laga kireeyo kabadhada qaadka, iyo dukaamada sharaabka iyo biyaha ay ka iibsadaan dadka qayilaa oo iyagana il dakhli si aan toos ahayn uga soo galo uu u yahay.

Joojinta qaadku waxa ay keenaysaa in miisaaniyaddii dawladda qaybtii ka iman jirtey qaadku meesha ka baxdo, taas oo keenaysa in mashaariicdii iyo adeegyadii bulsho ee dawladdu ku qaban lahayd meesha ka baxaan. Sidoo kale joojinta qaadku waxa ay keenaysaa in shaqo-abuurkii uu u samaynayay dadka sida tooska ah ugu tiirsan iyo kuwa aan sida tooska ah ugu tiirsanaynba lumo taas oo keenaysa kumanaan qof oo shaqaale ka ahaa ka ganacsiga geedkan in ay ilihii dakhligu kasoo galayay waayaan oo qoysaskii ku tiirsanaana xaalad dhaqaale-xumo soo foodsaarto iyo dhibaatooyinka kale oo badan.

Gebagabadii, in la qaado tallaabadan joojinta ahi maaha wax fudud oo dawlad iyo shacabba waa mid saamaynaysa, una baahan tashi qaran. Intaan la joojin waa in la helo ilo kale oo dhaqaale oo dawladda iyo shacbiga ku tiirsanba dakhli kasoo geli karo si looga baaqdo crises ay sababto tallaabadani.

Tanzania na Indonesia zimekubaliana kuendeleza zaidi ushirikiano wa kimaendeleo katika sekta mbalimbali za kiuchumi na kijamii ikiwemo kilimo na nishati kwa faida ya nchi hizo mbili. 

Hayo yamebainishwa jijini Dodoma, baada ya Waziri wa Fedha, Mhe. Balozi Khamis Mussa Omary (Mb), kukutana na kufanya mazungumzo na Balozi wa Indonesia nchini Tanzania, Tri Yogo Jatmiko.

Akizungumza katika kikao hicho, Mhe. Balozi Omar, ameishukuru Serikali ya Indonesia kwa mchango wake mkubwa katika kusaidia sekta mbalimbali za uchumi wa Tanzania ikiwemo sekta za madini, kilimo na mifugo tangu kuanzishwa kwa uhusiano wa kidiplomasia mwaka 1964.

“Mwaka huu ni maadhimisho ya miaka 62 tangu kuanzishwa kwa uhusiano wa kidiplomasia kati ya Tanzania na Indonesia, na uhusiano wetu umeendelea kuimarika zaidi kadiri miaka inavyosonga mbele, na pia tumeona ziara kati ya viongozi wetu Mhe. Dkt. Samia Suluhu Hassan, Rais wa Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania alipotembelea Indonesia, na Mhe. Prabowo Subianto Rais wa Indonesia alipokuja Tanzania, hii ni ishara ya uhusiano thabiti unaojengwa juu ya heshima na ushirikiano wa kweli,” alisema Mhe. Balozi Omar.

Aidha, Mhe. Balozi Omar alisema kuwa, dhamira ya Indonesia katika kukuza maendeleo endelevu na kupunguza umasikini imechangia kubadilisha kwa kiasi kikubwa maendeleo ya kijamii na kiuchumi nchini Tanzania kupitia misaada ya kifedha, ushauri wa kitaalamu, na programu za kujenga uwezo.

Aidha Mhe. Balozi Omar aliwaalika wawekezaji kutoka Indonesia kuja kuwekeza nchini katika sekta mbalimbali za kiuchumi na kijamii ikiwemo kilimo, uongezaji thamani wa mazao, madini, viwanda, nishati, miundombinu, afya, elimu na utalii.

Kwa upande wake, Balozi wa Indonesia nchini Tanzania, Mhe. Tri Yogo Jatmiko, alisema kuwa katika kuhakikisha kuwa nchi hizo zinadumisha ushirikiano zaidi ya Watanzania 170 wamepata manufaa kupitia programu hizo za kujenga uwezo katika sekta mbalimbali ikiwemo kilimo, mifugo, nishati, madini, uvuvi na fedha.

“Tutahakikisha tunaimarisha zaidi uhusiano huu kwa kuongeza kuwajengea uwezo wataalmu wa Tanzania ili maeneo yote tuliyokubaliana kushirikiana yanaleta tija na ustawi mpana wa uhusiano wa nchi hizi mbili,” alisema Mhe. Balozi Jatmiko.

Kikao hicho kilihudhuriwa pia na Naibu Katibu Mkuu Wizara ya Fedha, Bi. Amina Khamis Shaaban, Naibu Katibu Mtendaji wa Tume ya Mipango, Dkt. Blandina Kilama, Kamishna wa Idara ya Fedha za Nje Wizara ya Fedha, Bw. Rished Bade, Kamishna Msaidizi Idara ya Usimamizi wa Deni la Serikali, Bi. Tiba Kisonga na maafisa wengine waandamizi kutoka Wizara ya Fedha na ubalozi wa Indonesia nchini.

THE UNTOLD STORY OF THE KAMITI PRISON BREAK
How 3 terrorists embarrassed East Africa’s “most secure” prison.

On Mashujaa Day 2021, as President Uhuru Kenyatta announced the lifting of the night-to-dawn curfew, Kenyans celebrated freedom.

What nobody knew

That announcement didn’t just free citizens.
It completed an escape plan that had been cooking for months… behind the cold, unforgiving 10-foot walls of Kamiti Maximum Prison.

Deep inside Condemned Block A, Cell No. 6, three men were counting down their final hours as inmates.

The mission?
Escape Kamiti.

THE MEN BEHIND THE PLAN

Meet the masterminds:

-Musharaf Abdalla
-Juma Otieno (Yassin)
-Mohammed Ali Abikar

Certified Al-Shabaab operatives.
Hardened. Calculated. Desperate.

Musharaf and Yassin had been locked up since 2017 after attempting to storm Parliament Buildings in 2012—armed and ready. That stunt earned them 22 years at Kamiti Max.

Two years later, they were joined by Abikar, slapped with a massive 41-year sentence for communicating with the terrorists behind the Garissa University massacre that killed 147 students.

Later came Joseph Juma Odhiambo, arrested in Mandera while sneaking toward Somalia through an illegal border route. His reward? 15 years.

Different crimes. Same prison. Same bitterness.

“JUSTICE DELAYED…”

Despite courts proving their guilt beyond reasonable doubt, the four felt cheated.

Appeals dragged on.
Hope faded.
Anger brewed.

In their minds, justice delayed became justice denied.

So they agreed on one thing:
If the system wouldn’t free them, they’d free themselves.

ENTER: WARDEN X 

Step one? Compromise someone on the inside.

Using money Abikar could access from outside, they zeroed in on Warden X—the officer in charge of inmates doing routine maintenance.

Perfect target.

Why?

- He had access to tools
- He moved freely
- He knew duty rosters
- And he could pass information quietly

Soon, Warden X became their supply line, intelligence office

Hayo yamebainishwa jijini Dodoma, baada ya Waziri wa Fedha, Mhe. Balozi Khamis Mussa Omary (Mb), kukutana na kufanya mazungumzo na Balozi wa Indonesia nchini Tanzania, Mhe. Tri Yogo Jatmiko Avetisyan.

Akizungumza katika kikao hicho, Mhe. Balozi Omar, ameishukuru Serikali ya Indonesia kwa mchango wake mkubwa katika kusaidia sekta mbalimbali za uchumi wa Tanzania ikiwemo sekta za madini, kilimo na mifugo tangu kuanzishwa kwa uhusiano wa kidiplomasia mwaka 1964.

“Mwaka huu ni maadhimisho ya miaka 62 tangu kuanzishwa kwa uhusiano wa kidiplomasia kati ya Tanzania na Indonesia, na uhusiano wetu umeendelea kuimarika zaidi kadiri miaka inavyosonga mbele, na pia tumeona ziara kati ya viongozi wetu Mhe. Dkt. Samia Suluhu Hassan, Rais wa Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania alipotembelea Indonesia, na Mhe. Prabowo Subianto Rais wa Indonesia alipokuja Tanzania, hii ni ishara ya uhusiano thabiti unaojengwa juu ya heshima na ushirikiano wa kweli,” alisema Mhe. Balozi Omar.

Aidha, Mhe. Balozi Omar alisema kuwa, dhamira ya Indonesia katika kukuza maendeleo endelevu na kupunguza umasikini imechangia kubadilisha kwa kiasi kikubwa maendeleo ya kijamii na kiuchumi nchini Tanzania kupitia misaada ya kifedha, ushauri wa kitaalamu, na programu za kujenga uwezo.

Aidha Mhe. Balozi Omary aliwaalika wawekezaji kutoka Indonesia kuja kuwekeza nchini katika sekta mbalimbali za kiuchumi na kijamii ikiwemo kilimo, uongezaji thamani wa mazao, madini, viwanda, nishati, miundombinu, afya, elimu na utalii.

Kwa upande wake, Balozi wa Indonesia nchini Tanzania, Mhe. While I support the eradication of superstition and evil innovations in society, the solution is not to go all-out with takfīr and killing people Mongolian-style, like Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab did with the Arabian tribes.

That’s like the proverb:
الدواء أسوأ من الداء 
‘𝘈 𝘤𝘶𝘳𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘴𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘥𝘪𝘴𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘦.’

His followers say, “he didn’t bring anything new.”

Well, then we shouldn’t lose out on much if we discarded his words?

He was neither a Prophet, nor infallible. He was a man, sometimes right, sometimes wrong. Let God be his judge. 

True reform comes by educating people with kindness, evidences and reasoning, not by excommunicating and killing them.

🌟 Who are the Khawarij today and where are they found?

First, understand this rule clearly: Khawarij today are not identified by a single historical name. They are identified by their manhaj. Anyone who carries their beliefs is Khariji, even if he rejects the label.

🌟 Scholars identify modern Khawarij not by names, flags, or claims, but by their method and beliefs. A group is judged to be Khariji when it makes takfīr of Muslims over sins, political matters, or disagreements where Islam has allowed difference. This includes declaring Muslim rulers apostates without clear, open kufr proven by the Quran and Sunnah, and then using that claim to justify rebellion and bloodshed. When a group declares Muslim blood lawful, spreads chaos in Muslim lands, and presents disorder as Jihad or reform, this is a clear Khariji trait. Another defining sign is using the Quran without the Sunnah and without the understanding of the Salaf, taking verses in isolation and ignoring context, consensus, and scholarly principles. Such groups also show hostility toward recognized scholars, dismissing them as “scholars of the palace” or traitors, because true knowledge exposes their deviation. This is the scholarly measuring stick used by Ahl al-Sunnah. It is based on evidence and principles, not emotion, politics, or personal sympathy.

🌟 Modern groups that scholars classified as Khawarij

We are not guessing. This is the verdict of senior Salafi scholars like Ibn Bāz, al-Albānī, Ibn ʿUthaymīn, Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān, Rabīʿ al-Madkhalī and others.

❇️ Islamic State of Iraq and Syria, commonly known as ISIS or Dāʿish, operated mainly in Iraq and Syria and later spread cells into parts of Africa and Asia. Scholars identified this group as textbook Khariji because its actions and beliefs matched the classic Khariji pattern exactly. ISIS made mass takfīr of Muslims over sins, political issues, and disagreement, murdered scholars and civilians, and declared entire Muslim societies apostate. They justified these crimes by falsely labeling them as Jihad and claiming a so-called “khilāfah,” while completely ignoring the Quran, Sunnah, and the understanding of the Salaf. Their violence was directed primarily against Muslims, their rejection of scholars was absolute, and their chaos was presented as religion. Because of this clear alignment with Khariji doctrine and practice, scholars were united in classifying ISIS as Khariji, with no serious disagreement.

❇️ Al-Qaeda and its various branches emerged in places such as Yemen, Afghanistan, the Sahel region, and the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), usually in environments of war, political collapse, and weak religious guidance. While some of their early figures avoided openly declaring Muslims disbelievers, their methodology itself was flawed from the beginning. They built their actions on indirect takfīr by declaring rulers apostates, labeling entire systems as disbelief, and then treating anyone who worked within or lived under those systems as legitimate targets. This logic made Muslim blood “collateral damage” and gradually normalized the killing of Muslims under the excuse of necessity, strategy, or greater benefit. They also declared armed struggle without shari authority, without a recognized Muslim ruler, and without the conditions set by the Quran and Sunnah, which is a core Khariji principle. Over time, many of their branches moved from indirect takfīr to explicit takfīr, fully embracing Khariji beliefs and practices. This is why major scholars warned that even if some individuals spoke carefully, the path itself leads to Kharijism, because a corrupt foundation will always produce corrupt outcomes.

❇️ Boko Haram emerged mainly in Nigeria and later spread into Chad, Niger, and Cameroon, and its ideology is a clear continuation of the Khariji path. The group built its belief on blanket takfīr, declaring large parts of Muslim society disbelievers simply for living normal lives, sending children to school, or not joining their group. Anyone who disagreed with them, scholars, imams, parents, or ordinary Muslims, was labeled an apostate and killed. They went further by declaring schools, masajid, markets, and civilians lawful targets, carrying out bombings and mass killings. This behavior directly matches the classical Khariji pattern: misusing Quranic texts, rejecting scholars, rebelling without right, and spilling Muslim blood while claiming to defend Islam. There is nothing in their actions that aligns with Quran, Sunnah, or the understanding of the Salaf. Their manhaj is not jihad, not reform, and not resistance. It is pure Khariji violence, condemned by the Prophet ﷺ long before such groups appeared.

❇️ Takfīrī cells with no fixed name (the most dangerous form) - These takfīrī cells without a fixed name are the most dangerous form of modern Kharijism because they operate without structure, accountability, or visibility. They exist as Telegram groups, small armed cells, angry youth circles, and online “keyboard muftis” who issue takfīr and death verdicts from behind screens. They are spread across the Middle East, North Africa, South Asia, and even Europe and the West. Their danger lies in the fact that they do not need an organization to act; ideology alone is enough. They repeat the same slogans in every place and language: “the rulers are taghut,” “the scholars sold out,” “we follow Quran only,” and “whoever does not make takfīr is a kafir.” These phrases are not innocent. They are tools to strip Muslims of protection, cut people off from scholars, reject Sunnah and ijma, and slowly make Muslim blood feel permissible. This is pure Khariji DNA. Historically, this is exactly how the first Kharijis operated before becoming armies: isolation, self-righteousness, takfīr, then violence. Because these cells are decentralized, emotional, and fueled by ignorance, they spread faster than organized groups and cause immense harm while claiming religious purity.

❇️ Where Khariji thinking is most active today - Khariji ideology becomes most active in places where knowledge is weak and chaos is strong. It thrives in conflict zones torn by war, where fear, anger, and oppression replace learning and patience. In civil war environments, people look for quick answers and strong slogans, and Kharijis exploit this by offering simple but false solutions built on takfīr and violence. They also grow in societies where scholars are silenced, imprisoned, mocked, or pushed aside, because without scholars, there is no correct explanation of Quran and Sunnah. When people stop learning from qualified scholars, they start learning from emotions and weapons. In modern times, Khariji thinking has also moved heavily into online spaces, especially social media and private chat groups, where there is zero accountability, no correction, and no chain of knowledge. There, anonymous voices give fatwa, declare kufr, and glorify killing without fear of being questioned. This is exactly how Khariji ideology has always survived: it feeds on ignorance, anger, isolation, and the absence of trustworthy scholars. Wherever these conditions exist, the Khariji mindset finds fertile ground, even if the people carrying it deny the name.

❇️ They grow where ignorance spreads and people speak about Islam without knowledge, relying on slogans instead of Quran and Sunnah as understood by the Salaf. When emotions lead, anger replaces patience, and rage is treated as courage, people become easy targets for extremist ideas. They also grow where scholars are mocked or discredited, because once scholars are removed, there is no one left to explain the religion correctly, and loud voices take their place. And they thrive where unity is hated, because Khariji thinking survives on division, declaring others misguided, and breaking the Jamaah. Wherever knowledge is replaced with emotion, respect for scholars is replaced with suspicion, and unity is replaced with constant accusation, the Khariji mindset finds a home, even if the people carrying it refuse the name.

❇️ Straight verdict - Modern Khawarij do not look like the early Khawarij in clothing or setting, but they are identical in mindset and method. They speak modern language, use political terms, and spread their ideas through social media instead of desert camps. They use videos, slogans, and emotional narratives, sometimes waving black flags or catchy phrases that sound religious but lack real knowledge. Outwardly, they appear updated and organized, but inwardly their heart has not changed. It is still built on takfīr of Muslims, making blood lawful with ease, creating chaos in the name of reform, and showing arrogance toward scholars, rulers, and the wider Ummah. Just like the early Khawarij, they believe they alone represent truth, that disagreement equals disbelief, and that violence is a shortcut to righteousness. Different tools, same disease. The form changed, the poison did not.

❇️ The early history of the Khawarij clearly exposes their deviation through the way they constantly split into factions after the Battle of Nahrawan. Their first organized group was the Haruriyyah, named after Harura near Kufa, and from this root all later Khariji branches emerged. As time passed, their ideology did not stabilize but fractured further, producing groups like the Azāriqah, the most extreme and violent faction, who declared all Muslims outside their group disbelievers, permitted the killing of women and children, and labeled Muslim lands as Dār al-Kufr. The Najdat were slightly less extreme but still built their creed on takfīr of major sinners and armed rebellion. The Sufriyyah, who spread in North Africa, were inconsistent and internally contradictory, yet still shared the same foundation of takfīr. The Ibadiyyah were the least violent and survived until today in places like Oman and Zanzibar, but the early Salaf still classified them as Khariji in origin, because while their political behavior softened over time, the doctrinal root did not fully align with Ahl al-Sunnah. What unites all these factions is not mercy or reform, but agreement on takfīr and rebellion; they only differed on how much blood they allowed to be spilled. This endless fragmentation followed a clear pattern: first declaring major sinners disbelievers, then rulers, then Companions, then scholars, and finally ordinary Muslims, until they began making takfīr of one another, splitting over the smallest disagreements. This is why Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنه said they took verses revealed about disbelievers and applied them to believers, a misuse of the Quran that guaranteed division. Because of this reality, scholars like Ibn Taymiyyah stated plainly that the Kharijis were the first group to declare Muslims disbelievers, make their blood lawful, and rebel against Muslim leaders, and that they were more dangerous than other innovators because they combined false belief with bloodshed. Likewise, ʿAlī ibn Abī Talib رضي الله عنه, Imām Aḥmad, al-Ājurri, and Ibn ʿUmar all issued severe judgments against them, not as political reactions but as clear ʿaqīdah verdicts. Their history proves one rule without exception: truth unites, but innovation built on takfīr can only divide, fragment, and destroy.

👉 The Salaf were clear: Khawarij are the dogs of Hellfire, even if they pray all night and cry in dua.

❇️ Statements of the Salaf

Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله said: “The Khārijīs were the first to make takfīr of the Muslims and declare their blood lawful. and to rebel against the leaders of the Muslims.”

And he said:

“They are the first group to make takfīr of the Ummah, and by that they declared fighting them permissible.”

He also stated clearly:

“They are more evil than the Qadariyyah and Jahmiyyah, because they combine innovation with bloodshed.”

Imām Aḥmad رحمه الله said: “The Khārijīs are an evil people. No group is more evil than them.”

Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said: “They took verses revealed about disbelievers and applied them to believers.”

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه: “Do not fight the Khawarij after me. Whoever seeks the truth and errs is not like one who seeks falsehood and attains it.”
Meaning: they wanted truth but followed ignorance.

Al-Ājurri رحمه الله: “The Khārijīs are ignorant worshippers. They deceive themselves and others with Qur’an.”

Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما: “They are the worst of creation.”

These are not political statements. These are ʿaqīdah judgments. 

Sahih Hadith: Abu Ghalib narrated that Abu Umamah said: "(The Khawarij) are the worst of the slain who are killed under heaven, and the best of the slain are those who were killed by them. Those (Khawarij) are the dogs of Hell. Those people were Muslims but they became disbelievers." I said: "O Abu Umamah, is that your opinion?" He said: "Rather I heard it from the Messenger of Allah." - Sunan Ibn Majah 176.

NOTE: The Prophet ﷺ did not apply it to Jews, Christians, or idol worshippers, Hypocrites as a group He applied it to a Muslim sect because of their danger to the Ummah.

Abu Dharr reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:

Chers abonnés,

Ne ratez surtout pas l’intégralité de cette vidéo sur ma page Facebook demain matin, in châ’ Allâh.

Dans cet extrait, j’ai soulevé deux points fondamentaux, mais je dois insister avec fermeté sur un point précis : le takfîr.

Vous savez, les gens doivent impérativement faire la distinction claire et rigoureuse entre les sunnites et les Khawârij, ainsi qu’entre les jeunes se réclamant de la Sunna mais qui, par ignorance, portent l’idéologie des Khawârij. J’ai à maintes reprises expliqué le takfîr, les conditions du takfîr, ainsi que les personnes habilitées à accomplir ce travail, car cela n’est même pas confié à tous les savants, à plus forte raison aux étudiants, encore moins à nous, simples élèves en sciences islamiques.

Faisons donc extrêmement attention et sachons faire la part des choses entre le fait de juger l’acte d’un individu sans pour autant juger directement l’auteur de l’acte. C’est véritablement un chapitre d’une extrême sensibilité, qui mérite plusieurs années d’étude approfondie afin d’être traité avec justesse.

Les sunnites déclarent très rarement une personne spécifique comme étant mécréante ou hypocrite. Ils disent plutôt : tel acte est un acte de mécréance ou un acte d’hypocrisie, tout en considérant, dans le même temps, la personne comme musulmane, tant qu’elle n’a pas été déclarée mécréante par les juridictions islamiques, à travers des juges compétents ou des personnes désignées par une autorité légitime pour accomplir cette mission.

Ainsi, du moment où tu prends un texte à portée générale pour en tirer un jugement spécifique, tu as tout confondu. Et tu diras ensuite que c’est le Prophète Muhammad ﷺ lui-même qui l’a dit, ou qu’Allâh l’a dit. Certes, Allâh l’a dit, mais Allâh ou Son Prophète ont-ils mentionné le nom de la personne concernée ? Non. Il faut donc faire extrêmement attention ⚠️.

La charia islamique est d’une sensibilité extrême. Jugeons les actes sans suivre nos passions.

Pour mieux comprendre toutes ces explications, malgré les mises en garde répétées des savants sunnites contre les innovateurs, avez-vous déjà vu un savant refuser de prier sur l’un d’entre eux lorsqu’il décède ? Non, car agir ainsi revient à déclarer la personne mécréante.

Qu’Allâh nous guide. C’est un chapitre qui mérite beaucoup plus de détails, mais je m’arrête ici. Faisons simplement la distinction nécessaire entre les sunnites et les jeunes Khawârij sur les réseaux sociaux.

Continuity or Change? 🇺🇸✈️

​Ever wondered how much U.S. foreign policy actually shifts when the White House changes hands? While political rhetoric often highlights deep divides, the history of military engagements tells a more complex story of continuity.

​From the "Global War on Terror" to targeted drone strikes and strategic interventions, this map visualizes the footprint of the last four administrations. Whether it’s Bush, Obama, Trump, or Biden, the use of aerial operations has remained a central tool of American influence and security strategy across the globe.

​What do you think? Is this level of intervention necessary for global stability, or is it time for a new approach to diplomacy?

​👇 Let’s discuss in the comments.

​Detailed Analysis: Decades of Intervention

​The Evolution of American Air Power and Foreign Policy (2001–2026)

​For over two decades, the United States has maintained a posture of active military engagement that transcends partisan lines. While the domestic political landscape in America is often characterized by fierce debates between Republicans and Democrats, the application of kinetic military force—specifically through bombing and drone strikes—shows a remarkable level of institutional consistency. By examining the actions of Presidents George W. Bush, Barack Obama, Donald Trump, and Joe Biden, we can see how the "War on Terror" evolved from large-scale ground invasions to a more shadow-like, automated form of warfare that spans continents.

​The Bush Era: The Architect of the Forever Wars
The modern era of U.S. military interventionism was fundamentally shaped by the events of September 11, 2001. Under George W. Bush, the United States launched the "Global War on Terror," which began with the invasion of Afghanistan to dismantle Al-Qaeda and remove the Taliban. However, the scope quickly expanded. The 2003 invasion of Iraq marked a turning point, moving from a retaliatory strike to a pre-emptive doctrine of "regime change." During this period, the bombing campaigns were massive, aimed at destroying the infrastructure of the Ba'athist regime and later combatting a growing insurgency. Bush's legacy is defined by these two major fronts, but it also laid the groundwork for the expansion of strikes into Pakistan’s tribal areas, marking the infancy of the drone program.

​The Obama Era: The Drone President

When Barack Obama took office, he campaigned on the promise of ending the "dumb war" in Iraq. While he did oversee a withdrawal of troops, his administration oversaw a massive shift in how the U.S. projected power. The Obama era saw the "light footprint" strategy—trading thousands of boots on the ground for high-tech drone strikes and special operations. This period saw the expansion of bombing into several new theaters. In 2011, the U.S. played a pivotal role in the NATO-led intervention in Libya, which resulted in the fall of Muammar Gaddafi but left a power vacuum that persists today. Simultaneously, the Obama administration intensified strikes in Yemen and Somalia against Al-Shabaab and Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP). Despite receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, Obama remains the only president to have been at war for every day of an eight-year tenure, illustrating that "ending wars" often meant simply changing how they were fought.

​The Trump Era: Loosening the Rules of Engagement

Donald Trump’s "America First" platform suggested an isolationist shift, yet his administration actually saw an intensification of air strikes in several regions. In the fight against ISIS in Iraq and Syria, the Trump administration "decimated" the caliphate by significantly increasing the frequency of bombing runs. A key characteristic of this era was the loosening of "rules of engagement" designed to protect civilians, which led to a spike in reported casualties in places like Raqqa and Mosul. Trump also took a hardline stance against Iran, culminating in the 2020 drone strike that killed General Qasem Soleimani in Baghdad—an act that brought the two nations to the brink of direct war. Even in Afghanistan, the tonnage of bombs dropped reached record highs during his term, even as he negotiated a withdrawal with the Taliban.

​The Biden Era: Precision and Pivot

President Joe Biden oversaw the most significant symbolic end to the era of "Forever Wars" with the total withdrawal from Afghanistan in 2021. However, the map shows that "over-the-horizon" capabilities remain a core part of U.S. strategy. Under Biden, the U.S. has continued to conduct targeted strikes in Somalia against Al-Shabaab and has maintained a presence in Syria to counter ISIS remnants. Perhaps most notably, the Biden administration has engaged in a sustained bombing campaign in Yemen against Houthi rebels in response to attacks on international shipping in the Red Sea. This demonstrates that even when a president seeks to "pivot" away from the Middle East to focus on China or Russia, the regional instabilities often pull American air power back into the fray.

​The Human and Geopolitical Cost

The countries highlighted on this map—Pakistan, Yemen, Somalia, Libya, Iraq, Syria, and Afghanistan—represent a generation of conflict. For the USA audience, these interventions are often seen through the lens of national security and the prevention of terrorism on home soil. However, the geopolitical consequences are vast. These campaigns have contributed to massive migration waves toward Europe, the destabilization of entire regions, and a debate over the legality of executive war powers.

​In conclusion, the visual data suggests that while the rhetoric of American presidents varies wildly—ranging from Bush’s "freedom agenda" to Obama’s "hope," Trump’s "nationalism," and Biden’s "restoration of alliances"—the underlying mechanism of U.S. military reach remains consistent. The airplane and the drone have become the primary tools of American foreign policy, ensuring that regardless of who sits in the Oval Office, the reach of the U.S. military remains global and active.

Government of Somaliland
International Relationship
HomeInternational Relationship

The Republic of Somaliland is located in the Horn of Africa. It has the Gulf of Aden to the North and shares borders with Djibouti in the West, Ethiopia in the South and Somalia in the East. It has an area of 176,119 square Kilometers and a coastal line which stretches up to 800 Km along the Red Sea. In terms of area it would have ranked 37th in Africa, which means there are 18 countries with smaller areas than Somaliland in the continent. It is home to a population of four million. The capital, Hargeisa, is a metropolis with an estimated population of over one million. The national language is Somali but both English and Arabic are widely spoken.

INDEPENDENCE
Somaliland was officially proclaimed a British protectorate in 1887 after the conclusion of treaties between Great Britain and the various Somaliland clans. Its international boundaries were established by treaties and protocols between Britain, Ethiopia and France. Somaliland was granted its independence on June 26, 1960 by Royal proclamation of her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II. It was the 15th state to gain independence in the African continent. As many as thirty-five (35) states, including the permanent members of the Security Council acknowledged its independence immediately, and the United Kingdom signed several bilateral agreements with Somaliland which were deposited at the United Nations under article 102 of the UN Charter. The new state called the State of Somaliland was a fully-fledged sovereign state under international law. At independence in 1960, the State of Somaliland Constitution established a parliamentary system of government for Somaliland with a Government consisting of a Council of 5 ministers headed by a Prime Minister, a legislative assembly of 33 members and an Independent Judiciary. The Prime Minister Mr. Mohamed H I Egal was sworn as Prime Minister of the State of Somaliland on independence. He was not only the head of the Government but also the Commander in Chief of the Somaliland Army.

THE UNION
At the time of independence there was a strong anti-colonial sentiment sweeping the African continent. Somaliland was no exception. There was a popular drive to unite all the five Somali inhabited territories including Somaliland, Somalia, French Somaliland (Djibouti), Ogaden (Ethiopia), and the Northern Frontier District (NFD) of Kenya. The five-pointed white star on the flag symbolized this aspiration. The 1954 Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement in which Britain transferred 25,000 sq miles (64,750 sq km) of ‘Hawd’ grazing land to Ethiopia evoked an outcry in Somaliland and intensified the demand for a union to recover lost territory. Under public pressure, Somaliland and Somalia representatives opened a dialogue on a union between the two territories. The two parties agreed to sign an act of Union after independence. They agreed that the act would be in the nature of an international agreement between two states. Accordingly, the Legislative Assembly of the independent State of Somaliland approved and signed the Union of Somaliland and Somalia Law on 27 June 1960. The Law was immediately effective in Somaliland, but as set out in the recital, it was supposed to be signed by the representatives of Somalia, as well. In fact, this never happened. Instead, the Legislative Assembly of the Somalia Trust Territory met on 30 June 1960 and decided to approve “in principle” an Act of Union (Atto di Unioni), which was significantly different from the Act of Union drafted by Somaliland assembly. According to Contini, (The Somali Republic: An Experiment in Legal Integration, Frank Cass & Co. Lt 1969: London), the Assembly requested the “Government of Somalia to establish with the Government of Somaliland a definitive single text of the Act of Union, to be submitted to the National Assembly for approval”.

But on the morning of 1st July 1960, the members of the Somaliland Legislative (33) and those of the Somalia Legislative (90) met in a joint session and the Constitution which was drafted in Somalia was accepted on the basis of an acclamation, with no discussion, and a Provisional President was elected. The newly elected Provisional President issued on the same day a decree aiming to formalize the union, but even that was never converted into Law as presidential decrees always require to be presented to the National Assembly for conversion into Law under Article 63(3) of the new Constitution within five days of their publication, otherwise, they shall cease to have effect from their date of issue. Thus, although the agreement between Somaliland and Somalia was that the same Act of Union would be signed by both states, that did not happen and the legal formalities were not completed properly as agreed. According to Contini,

“the Union of Somaliland and Somalia Law did not have any legal validity in the South (Somalia) and the approval “in principle” of the Atto di Unione was not sufficient to make it legally binding in that territory.”

Cotran [(1968)12 ICLQ 1010] comments that the legal validity of the legislative instruments establishing the union was “questionable” and he summarized the reasons as follows:

The Union of Somaliland and Somalia Law, and the Somalia Act of Union were both drafted in the form of bilateral agreements, but neither of them was signed by the representatives of the two territories.
The Union of Somaliland and Somalia Law purported to derogate in some respects from the Constitution of the Somali Republic.
The Somalia Act of Union was approved “in principle” but never enacted into law.
The decree law of July 1, 1960, did not come into effect since it was not converted into law in accordance with the Constitution.”
It was only on 18 January 1961 when a new Act of Union was put to the National Assembly and was promulgated on 31 January 1961. This Law entitled the “Act of Union” was made retrospective even though there is a generally accepted principle that laws should not be retroactive. The new Act of Union was different from the one signed by the Somaliland Legislature. The Law of Union passed by the Somaliland Legislature contained some guarantees about the laws applicable in Somaliland, the rights of Somaliland serving officers, which should not become less favorable than was applicable to them at the time of the union, the establishment of a special Commission on laws and its composition etc. These were, in hindsight, the only, rather halfhearted, demands that Somaliland made at the time of the union. But the 1961 retrospective Act was very clear in repealing anything which was inconsistent with the 1960 Somalia Constitution, and specifically repealed “the provisions of the Union of Somaliland and Somalia (Law No.1 of 1960)” except for Article 11(4) which relates to agreements entered into by the independent State of Somaliland (see Article 9(2) of the 1961 Act of Union).

The above is a clear indication that Somaliland was an independent state with a Government of its own, however short lived. This was again confirmed by Article 11(4) of the 1961 Act of Union, which read:

“all rights lawfully vested in or obligations lawfully incurred by the independent Governments of Somaliland and Somalia … shall be deemed to have been transferred to and accepted by the Somali Republic upon its establishment”.

On 20 June 1961 a constitutional referendum was held to vote on the new constitution for the country created the previous year by the union of British Somaliland and Italian Somalia. The constitution was overwhelmingly approved by Somalia voters. But, in Somaliland, the referendum was boycotted by the leading political party, the Somali National League (SNL), as a result only 100,000 votes were casted, and 60% of those voted opposed the provisional constitution.

POST UNION
The displeasure with the union by the people of Somaliland manifested itself not only at the polling stations but also in the form of an attempted military coup by young officers from Somaliland in December 1960. The aim was to restore Somaliland sovereignty. The coup failed and the leading officers were tried in a court in Mogadishu. The proceedings started in 1963. The judge was Mr. Hazelwood from the court of Hargeisa and the prosecutor was an Italian. The trial took two months and the prisoners were acquitted. The judge declared that there was no case for the following reasons:

The officers were never sworn for a country called ‘Somali Republic and The trial could not be conducted under the constitution of Somali Republic; it should be conducted under the State of Somaliland jurisdiction.
The Union turned out to be problematic. The two countries were different in many ways. the administrative systems were different
The legal systems were different
The educational systems were different
The working languages (English and Italian) were different
The civil servant culture and ethics were different
The UN created in 1960 the Consultative Commission for integration, an international board headed by Paolo contini, to guide the gradual merger of the two new country’s legal systems and institutions and to SOMALILAND AN INTERNATIONAL CASE MoFA&IC reconcile the difference between them. But the differences were not limited to systems. There were big gaps in the people’s mindset and expectations, and the people of Somaliland soon became disillusioned. They felt marginalized and reduced to second class citizens. In the first government formed in 1960 by Adan Abdalla Osman, all the key portfolios went to people who hailed from Somalia including:

The President – Mr. Adan Abdallah Osman
The Prime Minister – Mr. Abdirashid Ali Sharmarke
Interior Minister – Abdirizaq H Hussein
Minister of Foreign Affairs - Abdillahi Esse
The speaker of the house of parliament – Haji Bashir Ismail Yousuf
The Chief Justice – Dr. Haji Nuur Mohamed (1962)
The commander of the army – Colonel Daud Abdillahi Hersi
Police commissioner – Mohamed abshir Muse
The capital and the seat of the government - Mogadishu
Cabinet positions – 11 out of 14
The inequalities manifested in many other ways. In the national assembly Somalia had 90 seats, where Somaliland had only 33 seats. The six districts of Somaliland at independence (Borama, Hargeisa, Bernera, Burao, Erigavo and Las Anood) were reduced to two regions (Hargeisa and Burao), while the six districts of Somalia at independence (Miguirtinia, Mudug, Hiran, Banaadir, Alto Jubba, Basso Juba) were all elevated to regional jurisdictions. Somalilanders were bypassed in a wave of promotions after independence, and Job opportunities became available to only those with the right connections in Mogadishu.

The union was not between equals. The feeling was not mutual. The enthusiasm for Somali nationalism and unity were not shared. Mohamud Abdi Nur, a Somalia politician warned Mr. Mohamed Haji Ibrahim Egal against a hasty Union and the lurking perils. In a letter to Mr. Egal he said:

‘There is no Somali Nationalism felt here in Somalia. My advice to you is to abandon the pursuit of a union with Somalia. If that is difficult, then I would suggest that you claim to occupy the same positions the British are currently holding under the UN Somali Trusteeship, so as to secure a share of the power when the two countries unite. Also, request a quota for the number of MPs you want to have in Parliament. Write down what you expect in terms of sharing power with the leadership in Somalia before you join. Otherwise you will be facing disappointment in the future as the people here do not have the same mind-set and no feeling for Somali brotherhood’

Unfortunately, Mr. Nur’s counsel was not headed and his prophesy materialized. As a mark of protest against the severing of diplomatic ties with the UK on the question of NFD, Egal resigned from the cabinet in 1963; formed a new political party, the Somali National Congress, and remained the leader of the Parliament in Opposition until 1965.

The situation got worse after the president, Mr. Abdirashid Ali Sharmarke was assassinated on the 15th of October 1969 and his government lead by the prime minister, Mr. Mohamed Haji Ibrahim Egal was overthrown by the Military in a coup de’ eta masterminded by General Siyad Bare on 21st October 1969.

The military Junta adopted what it called ‘scientific socialism’. It suspended the constitution, banned political parties, dissolved the parliament, disbanded the Supreme Court, curtailed all political freedoms and nationalized the financial institutions, almost all industries and trade. This affected everybody, but particularly the people of Somaliland who were traditionally entrepreneurs who depended on the private sector for their livelihoods. The economic marginalization of the northern regions (Somaliland) also extended to the distribution of development aid. It is estimated that the North received less than 7% of nationally disbursed development assistance by late 1970s. At least 93% of all development projects and scholarships were distributed to the South.

The regime passed legislation giving the state wide powers of detention and execution to a number of paramilitaries, militias and security agencies including the national Security Services (NSS), the Military Police (Hangash), and the Victory Pioneers (Guul wadayaal). High security prisons such as ‘Laanta Buuran’ and ‘labaatan Jirow’ where political dissidents were incarcerated were built with the help of communist East Germany. One of the inmates was Mr. Mohamed Haji Ibrahim Egal who symbolized Somaliland. He was kept in jail for 6 years from 1969 to October 1975, and was rearrested a year later in 1976 to serve another 6 years.

In 1977 the regime declared war on Ethiopia in an attempt to conquer Ogaden, the Somali inhabited region of Ethiopia. After initial successes, the Soviet Union which was the mainstay of the Somali national army switched sides, by abandoning the regime and supporting Ethiopia along with Cuba. As a result, the Somali army was defeated in 1978. This lead to three major developments:

Massive economic crises

One million Somali refugees fleeing Ethiopia, of which about 400,000 were settled in 11 camps in the North Western regions (Somaliland)

Discontent among the army

The Barre regime became increasingly paranoid, oppressive and violent. The execution of 82 high level military officers executed for their opposition to the way the war was handled prompted an attempted Coup de eta in April 1978. The reaction was a major crackdown on individuals and communities perceived to be hostile to the government. The refugees in the camps were armed to support the army against the local community which welcomed them to their homes not long ago. The people could not take it any longer and started to resist.

WAR AND CRIME
In response to the targeted harsh policies enacted by Siad Barre against the people of Somaliland, a group of social and political activists established the Somali National Movement (SNM) in April 12 1981 in London. By 1982, The SNM, transformed into a liberation front which engaged the Somali National Army in hit and run operations. The government took revenge on the people for the SNM activities. According to 1990 Africa Watch report,

‘Both the urban population and the nomads living in the country side have been subjected to summary killings, arbitrary arrest, detention in squalid conditions, torture, rape, crippling constraints on freedom of movement and expression and a pattern of psychological intimidations. ‘

On May 27, 1988, the SNM launched a surprise attack on Burao, followed by another attack on Hargeisa on May 31. The operation was successful against all odds and the movement managed to hold onto parts of the two cities for days. The government responded with a massacre of the civilian population. The number of civilian deaths in the ensued carnage is estimated between 50,000- 100,000. The government attacks included the leveling and complete destruction of Hargeisa through a campaign of aerial bombardment. This has lead to more than 400,000 people fleeing their homes and crossing borders to seek sanctuary in refugee camps in Ethiopia. Another 400, 000 became internally displaced. The infamous letter, ‘the Final Solution’, written by General Mohamed Saed Hirsi, the commander of the 26th regiment in the ‘North’ (Somaliland) to Siyad Bare, on January 17, 1978 revealed the intention of the regime to eliminate the majority community in Somaliland.

In 2001, the United Nations commissioned an investigation on past human rights violations in Somalia, specifically to find out if "crimes of international jurisdiction (i.e. war crimes, crimes against humanity or genocide) had been perpetrated during the country's civil war". The investigation was commissioned jointly by the United Nations Co-ordination Unit (UNCU) and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The investigation concluded with a report confirming the crime of genocide to have taken place against the Isaaqs (the majority community) in Somalia.

RECONCILIATION
After the liberation of the country and the collapse of the regime in Mogadishu, the people of Somaliland embarked on a series reconciliation conferences including:

February 1991 Berbera conference
April-May 1991 Burao conference
October 1992 Sheikh conference
Jan-May 1993 Borama conference
September 1996 Beer conference
October 1996- February 1997 Hargeisa conference
These meetings were attended by representatives of a broad spectrum of the community including traditional leaders, religious leaders, SNM leadership, politicians, intellectuals, businessmen, and members from the Diaspora community. The main purpose was to make peace, resolve conflict, reconcile differences, build confidence, demobilize militias, and transit from SNM based governance structure to a broader community/clan-based system. These conferences laid the foundation for the new Somaliland state.

DEMOCRACY AND STATE BUILDING
Collective decision-making is part of the tradition of Somaliland. The SNM, the precursor to the Somaliland government, was an inclusive democratic institution that changed leadership democratically five times in a span of 10 years. That tradition was carried on by the successive governments that ensued.

On May 28, 1991, Abdirahman Ahmed Ali Tuur was elected the first president of Somaliland by delegates and was sworn in as president on June 7, 1991.

On May 5, 1993, Mohammad Ibrahim Egal was elected president of Somaliland at Borama conference and was inaugurated as president on May 16, 1993. The National Charter, the precursor of the Somaliland constitution, was adopted.

On February 23, 1997, President Mohammad Ibrahim Egal was re-elected by the National Communities Conference (meeting as an electoral college), and an interim constitution was approved.

On 31 May 2001, the present Somaliland constitution was put to a referendum. 97.9% of electorate voted for the new constitution referendum endorsed by international observers as free and fair.

On May 3, 2002, President Egal died in Pretoria, South Africa, and Vice-President Dahir Riyale Kahin was sworn in as president of Somaliland on May 4, 2002

On December 15, 2002 the first Local elections were held SOMALILAND AN INTERNATIONAL CASE MoFA&IC

On April 14, 2003, President Dahir Riyale Kahin of the United Peoples’ Democratic Party (Ururka Dimuqraadiga Ummadda Bahawday – UDUB) was re-elected

On September 29, 2005, the first Legislative elections were held. The election was declared free and fair by a South African-led non-governmental mission consisting of 76 observers from 12 countries.

On June 26, 2010, Ahmed Mahamoud Silanyo of Kulmiye party was elected president and was inaugurated as president on July 27, 2010. This was the second presidential election by popular vote. The election was declared free and fair by more than 70 international observers.

On November 28, 2012, the second Local elections were held. 50 international election observers from 17 countries monitored the local elections which were declared free and fair

On November 13, 2017, the third presidential election was held. Muse Behi Abdi of Kulmiye part was elected and was inaugurated on December 13, 2017. 60 observers from 27 countries declared that they have witnessed a poll that preserved the integrity of the electoral process.

STATEHOOD
Somaliland fulfils all the requirements of a Statehood according to 1933 Montevideo Convention. It has:

A permanent population, estimated at 4 million.

A defined Territory with a total area of 176,200 Sq Km. demarcated by international borders established by protocols and treaties. Specifically, by:

The Anglo-French treaty of 1888
The Anglo-Italian protocol of 1894
The Anglo Ethiopian treaty of 1897
The capacity to enter into relations with Sovereign states, international corporations, agencies and organizations. It has already signed multiple MOUs, agreements, leases and concessions with countries and companies.

Somaliland has a democratically elected president, a democratically elected parliament and democratically elected local councilors. It has its own:

Constitution
Flag
Passport
Central bank
Money
Army and
Courts
It has representatives in more than 20 countries, and there are growing numbers of foreign consulates and representative offices in operation in Somaliland.

RECOGNITION
Somaliland is not a new state. It is an old state. It was a British protectorate for 73 years, gained its sovereignty from Britain 58 years ago, and it has been a fully functioning state for the past s27 years. The state of Somaliland is not an aspiration; it is a reality and enjoys a de facto recognition. It abides by international laws and protocol norms. It takes very seriously its duties and responsibilities as a member of the international community.

Before it joined Somalia, Somaliland was an independent sovereign state. The union though faulty was a voluntary union between two independent states. The union did not work. It brought death and destruction and ended in tears. The people of Somaliland demonstrated their unhappiness with the Union right from the start. They voted down the union constitution devised by Somalia in 1961; a coup de eta was attempted by young Somaliland officers in the same year; and a ten-year liberation war was fought from 1981 to 1991. The war was costly. Somaliland lost 50,000-100,000 citizens in the hands of the Somali national army, which carried out a scorch earth military campaign with the expressed intention to exterminate communities. Yet, no one has been convicted for the crimes against humanity committed.

The people of Somaliland decided at the Grand Conference in Burao in 1991 to leave the union and reclaim their independence. That was neither the first time nor the last time African states entered into a union to be dissolved later.

In 1958, Syria and Egypt created a political union, the United Arab Republic (AR), which was subsequently dissolved in 1961

In June 1960, French Sudan and Senegal united as Mali and separated in August 1960

In 1980, Senegal and Gambia formed Sengambia and then parted their ways in 1989

In 1950 The UN federated Eritrea with Ethiopia but the two countries separated following a UN monitored referendum in 1993

‘The Union established in 1960 brought enormous injustice and suffering to the people of the region. Objectively viewed, the case should not be linked to the notion of ‘opening a Pandora Box’. As such the AU should find a special method of dealing with this outstanding case.’

The findings of the AU mission were echoed in a 2006 report by the International Crises Group which said:

‘The African Union Challenge is to provide timely, neutral leadership in order to ensure a just, peaceful and enduring settlement, before confrontation and violence becomes the only option imaginable by both parties…. The above testimony shows clearly that Somaliland has a historic, political, legal and humanitarian case and right to be recognized. El Adde: 15 January 2016.
In the early hours of Friday, 15 January 2016, before sunrise touched the dusty plains of El Adde, Somalia, a Kenyan flag fluttered quietly above a KDF camp that had stood there for years as part of the AMISOM mission.

It was around 5:30 a.m.
Most soldiers were just waking up.
Some were preparing for morning routines.
Some were thinking of home — of families in Kenya who believed the worst days were behind them.

Then the ground exploded.
A massive suicide vehicle bomb slammed into the camp gates, tearing through defenses built to withstand gunfire, not betrayal of dawn. Within moments, Al-Shabaab fighters poured in, launching one of the deadliest attacks ever faced by the Kenya Defence Forces.

The battle that followed was brutal and uneven.
On that morning of 15 January 2016, Kenyan soldiers fought with discipline and courage under overwhelming pressure. Communication lines failed. Ammunition ran low. Smoke and dust blurred friend from foe. Yet they held positions, protected each other, and resisted for hours.
Some were wounded and still fought.
Some shielded fellow soldiers with their own bodies.
Some never made it out.
By mid-morning, El Adde camp had been overrun.
Back in Kenya, the date would soon be etched into memory.

Families began hearing whispers. Phones went unanswered. The government confirmed that Kenyan soldiers had been killed, though exact numbers were not immediately released. Grief spread faster than official statements.

Mothers waited.
Wives hoped.
Children asked questions no one could answer.
In the days that followed, Kenya mourned quietly and painfully. The fallen were not just soldiers,they were young men who had deployed years earlier to protect a nation they loved, far from its borders.
El Adde, once a remote Somali town few Kenyans knew, became a symbol of sacrifice, loss, and unanswered questions.

To this day, 15 January 2016 remains one of the darkest dates in Kenya’s military history, #kdf youare our heroes

Saxaabigii Khaalid ibnu Waliid:

Taliyaha ugu weyn ee militariga taariikhda, qabsashadii Faaris iyo Roomaanka, waligiis lagama guulaysan dagaal. Nebi Muxamed (nabadgelyo korkiisa ha ahaatee) wuxuu ugu yeeri jiray Seeftii La Qaaday ee Ilaah.

Khaalid ibnu Waliid (Ilaahay ha ka raalli noqdee), Saaxiibkii sharafta lahaa, guulaystihii weynaa, iyo taliyihii ciidanka ee guuleystay, ayaa geeriyooday.

Tani waxay dhacday 23-kii Muxaram, 21-kii Hijriyada (oo u dhiganta Janaayo 1, 642 Miilaadiga).

Wuxuu ahaa Abu Sulayman Khalid ibnu Waliid al-Makhzumi al-Qurayshi, oo caan ku ahaa qorsheyntiisa milatari ee cajiibka ah, xirfaddiisa hoggaaminta ciidamada, iyo guulihii uu ka gaaray Dagaalladii Ridda iyo qabsashadii Ciraaq iyo Levant xilligii khilaafadii Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (Ilaahay ha ka raalli noqdee) iyo Cumar ibnu Khattab (Ilaahay ha ka raalli noqdee).

Waxaa loo arkaa mid ka mid ah taliyayaashii militariga ee taariikhda oo aan waligood lagu jabin dagaal noloshiisa oo dhan. Wuxuu ku guulaystay in ka badan boqol dagaal oo uu la galay ciidamo tiro ahaan ka sarreeya Boqortooyadii Roomaanka ee Byzantine, Boqortooyadii Faaris ee Sasanian, iyo xulafadooda. Sannado yar gudahood, wuxuu awooday inuu dib u sawiro khariidadda adduunka isagoo ka adkaaday labada boqortooyo ee ugu awoodda badan oo beddelay taariikhda.

Part 3

Nineteen Kenyan citizens, an American and a British-South African man died during the attack.

On the same day, the Australian embassy denied allegations that one of the fatalities was an Australian. Initially both Kenyan and Australian media houses had stated that one of the victims was an Australian citizen and was visiting his girlfriend in Kenya before his death in the attack.

Five men are believed to have carried out the massacre. Two of the attackers were ethnic Kenyans, while the other three were Somali. 

Within days of the attack, the Kenyan government had released the names of two of the attackers and was able to confirm the identity of a third attacker but withheld their name, while the other two Somali attackers weren't identified until December 2020 following Al-Shabaab's media wing, Al-Kataib, releasing a film showing them in the days prior to the attack. 

Ali Salim Gichunge (born 1995), also known as Abu Sakeena, was the operational leader of the attack. 

He was born in Isiolo to a Muslim Kikuyu family, with his father being a serving KDF soldier. He studied at Hekima Primary from nursery to Standard Six. He sat his Kenyan Certificate of Primary Education exam in 2007 and scored 355 out of 500 possible marks. 

After graduating secondary school at Thuura Boys High School in 2011, he studied IT and was hired by a local hotel to manage its internet cafe.

In early 2016, Gichunge informed his family that he had begun working at a construction site in Mombasa after being invited to do so by a friend, however the friend told the family a month later that he had lost all contact with him. 

Gichunge then told his family that he had begun studying Islam in Uganda. In 2017, he contacted his family saying that he was in Lamu to leave the country, but said he would return soon, however the family did not hear from him for two years.

Mahir Khalid Riziki, (born 5 February 1993), also known as Jibril, was the suicide bomber who blew himself up at the Secret Garden Restaurant on 14 Riverside Drive. He was born and brought up in Majengo area of Mombasa, and was a known extremist with a history of violence. 

He had been a frequent attender at the Musa Mosque, a place commonly associated for nearly a decade as a key radicalization and recruitment center for Al-Shabaab, where he met Ramadhan Hamisi Kufungwa, a recruiter and member of Al-Shabaab.

In October 2014, Mahir was implicated in the killing of a police officer in Mombasa and following a warrant for his arrest, he fled to Tanzania in November 2014. 

By early 2015, he had told his family that he was now in Somalia training with Al-Shabaab. Just two days before the attack, on January 13, 2019, Riziki had re-entered Kenya through El-Wak in Mandera Country, and took a bus to Nairobi to link up with the attack cell leader, Ali Salim Gichunge, and to obtain instructions on what his part in the attack would be. He blew himself up just 48 hours later.

Osman Ahmed Hassan, (born 1992), also known as Azzam, was one of the gunman involved in the attacks. He was born in Wajir, Kenya and was of the Degodia tribe. 

He allegedly received no formal education and was a mechanic. The video released by Al-Shabaab in 2020 shows him speaking to the other attackers in both Swahili and Somali in an apartment block in Nairobi, as a video of Osama Bin Laden plays in the background.

Muhammed Adam Nur, also known as Farhaan Yare, was one of the gunmen involved in the attacks. He was born in Somalia and was of the Hadame tribe.

Abdulqani Arab Yusuf, another gunman, also known as Farhaan Dheere, was born in Somalia and was of the Muhammed Zubayr sub-clan of the Ogaden clan.

Buugga How Europe Underdeveloped Africa oo uu qoray aqoonyahanka taariikhda iyo dhaqaalaha Walter Rodney, kuna soo baxay 1972, waa mid ka mid ah qoraallada ugu miisaanka culus ee si qoto dheer u falanqeeya xidhiidhka taariikheed ee ka dhexeeya Yurub iyo Afrika. Buuggan wuxuu si cilmiyeed u diiddan yahay aragtida sheegaysa in Afrika ay dib-u-dhacday sababo dabiici ah awgood, isaga oo caddeynaya in dibu dhacaasi uu ahaa natiijo toos ah oo ka dhalatay gumaysigii Yurub iyo nidaamkii caalamiga ahaa ee caddaalad-darrada ku dhisnaa.

𝐆𝐮𝐦𝐚𝐲𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐚 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐃𝐢𝐛-𝐮-𝐝𝐡𝐚𝐜𝐚 𝐃𝐡𝐚𝐪𝐚𝐚𝐥𝐞
Walter Rodney wuxuu buuggiisa ku muujinayaa in gumaysigu uusan ahayn oo keliya qabsasho dhul, balse uu ahaa hannaan dhaqaale oo si nidaamsan u curyaamiyay awooddii wax-soo-saar ee Afrika. Kheyraadkii dabiiciga ahaa, sida macdanta, beeraha, iyo shaqaalihii Afrika, waxaa si joogto ah loogu leexiyay Yurub, halka Afrika laga dhigay suuq u furan badeecooyinka shisheeye. Nidaamkan ayaa burburiyay warshadihii yaryaraa ee Afrika, isla markaana ka dhigay qaaradda mid ku tiirsan dibadda.

𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐨𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐚 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐁𝐮𝐫𝐛𝐮𝐫𝐤𝐚 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐝𝐚
Mid ka mid ah qodobbada ugu culus ee buuggu taabanayo waa addoonsigii Afrika. Rodney wuxuu ku doodayaa in addoonsigu uu ahaa musiibo bani’aadannimo iyo dhaqaale oo aan weligeed laga soo kaban. Malaayiin Afrikaan ah oo ahaa xoog-shaqo firfircoon ayaa laga kaxaystay qaaradda, taas oo keentay hoos u dhac ku yimid horumarkii bulsho, wax-soo-saarkii dhaqaalaha, iyo isku-xidhkii bulshada. Addoonsigu wuxuu sidoo kale abuuray kala qaybsanaan iyo nuglaansho weli saamayn ku leh Afrika maanta.

𝐒𝐢𝐲𝐚𝐚𝐬𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐚, 𝐖𝐚𝐱𝐛𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐝𝐚, 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐌𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐚𝐱-𝐠𝐮𝐦𝐚𝐲𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐚
Buuggu wuxuu sidoo kale iftiiminayaa sida gumaysigu u saameeyay nidaamyadii siyaasadeed iyo waxbarasho ee Afrika. Waxbarashada gumaysiga looma qaabayn si loo horumariyo bulshada Afrika, balse waxay ujeedadeedu ahayd in la abuuro dad u hoggaansan danaha gumaysatada. Sidaas darteed, hoggaamiyeyaal badan oo Afrikaan ah ayaa ku soo barbaaray aragtiyo shisheeye oo aan u adeegin danaha shacabka ay hoggaaminayeen.

Yurub ma horumarin lahayn sida ay maanta tahay haddii aysan ka faa’iidaysan kheyraadka, shaqaalaha, iyo suuqyada Afrika. Sidaas awgeed, buuggu wuxuu ku baaqayaa in dib loo eego sheekada caalamiga ah ee horumarka, lana aqoonsado doorka gumaysigu ku lahaa sinnaan-la’aanta maanta jirta.

Buuggu wuxuu Afrika ku dhiirrigelinayaa in ay dib u fahanto taariikhdeeda, si ay u dhisato mustaqbal ku salaysan is-ku-filnaansho, cadaalad, iyo madax-bannaani dhab ah. Muqdisho 23ka Diseembar 2025 Gudniinka Fircooniga ah (FGM) waxaa caalamka si rasmi ah loogu aqoonsan yahay xadgudub ka dhan ah xuquuqda aadanaha, caafimaadka, iyo badqabka jirka ee gabdhaha iyo haweenka.
Dhawaan magaalada Baydhabo, UNTMIS iyo UNICEF  ayaa taageeray aqoon-is-weydaarsi wacyigelin ah oo socday 4 maalmood, kaas oo ay soo qabanqaabisay Wasaaradda Haweenka, Arrimaha Qoyska iyo Xuquuqda Aadanaha ee Dowlad-goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed, looguna talagalay 60 xildhibaan oo ka tirsan baarlamaanka dowlad-goboleedkaas.
Xildhibaanadu waxay ballan-qaadeen inay taageerayaan ansixinta hindise-sharciyeedka ka dhanka ah gudniinka fircooniga ah (FGM) iyo hindise-sharciyeedka Xuquuqda Carruurta, iyagoo u aqoonsaday tallaabooyin taariikhi ah oo muhiim u ah daryeelka, xuquuqda, iyo fayo-qabka haweenka, gabdhaha, iyo carruurta.
Waqooyu Barri 23ka Diseembar 2025 Wasiirka Warfaafinta Maamulka Waqooyi Bari Soomaaliya, Ahmed Cabdirisaaq Diiriye, ayaa si adag u beeniyay hadal uu dhawaan jeediyay xildhibaan ka tirsan Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya, kaas oo sheegay in Maamulka Waqooyi Bari uusan ku jirin miisaaniyadda dowladda federaalka ee sanadkan.
Wasiirka ayaa sheegay in hadalkaasi uu yahay mid aan sal iyo raad toona lahayn, islamarkaana uu ka fog yahay xaqiiqada dhabta ah. Wuxuu xusay in ay jiraan dadaallo rasmi ah oo iskaashi ah oo u dhexeeya hay’adaha maaliyadda ee dowladda federaalka iyo maamulka Waqooyi Bari, kuwaas oo uu sheegay inay marayaan meel wanaagsan.
“Waxaan ugu baaqayaa xildhibaanka hadalkaas sheegay inuu si cad u soo bandhigo bogga ama dukumeentiga uu ka akhriyey in Waqooyi Bari laga reebay miisaaniyadda, maaddaama miisaaniyadda qaranku aysan ku dhisnayn qabiil ama gobol gaar ah, balse ay ku socoto habraac sharci iyo mid maamul,” ayuu yiri wasiirku.
Wasiirka Warfaafinta ayaa sidoo kale tilmaamay in miisaaniyadda dowladda federaalka ay marto nidaam sharci ah oo Baarlamaanka Federaalka ansixiyo, islamarkaana mas’uuliyadda gaarsiinteeda ay saaran tahay dowlad-goboleedyada, iyadoo loo marayo hannaan rasmi ah.
Wasiirku wuxuu xusuusiyay xildhibaannada kasoo jeeda Waqooyi Bari in ay leeyihiin masuuliyad wadareed oo ku aaddan difaaca danaha deegaankooda iyo ummaddooda, isla markaana looga baahan yahay inay ka fogaadaan hadallo keeni kara jahwareer iyo kala qaybsanaan bulsho.
Maraykanka 23ka Diseembar 2025 Dowladda Mareykanka ayaa dib ugu yeertay ku dhowaad 30 dublamaasi oo sare, kuwaas oo uu ku jiro Safiirka Mareykanka ee Soomaaliya, tallaabadan oo qeyb ka ah dib-u-habeyn lagu sameynayo siyaasadda dibadda ee Mareykanka, si ay ula jaanqaaddo ajendaha “America First”.
Sida ay sheegeen saraakiil ka tirsan Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Mareykanka, madaxda safaaradaha ee ugu yaraan 29 dal ayaa toddobaadkii hore lagu wargeliyay in xilalkooda ay dhammaanayaan bisha Janaayo ee soo socota. Diblamaasiyiintan ayaa dhammaantood xilalka la wareegay xilligii madaxweyne Joe Biden.
Qaaradda Afrika ayaa ah tan ugu saameynta badan, iyadoo safiirro laga qaaday 13 dal, oo ay ka mid tahay Soomaaliya, Nigeria, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, Uganda iyo dalal kale.
Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Mareykanka ayaa difaacday tallaabadan, iyadoo sheegtay in safiirku yahay wakiil gaar ah oo madaxweynaha matala, isla markaana uu madaxweynuhu xaq u leeyahay inuu doorto shaqsiyaad si buuxda u taageeraya siyaasaddiisa.
Inkasta oo safiirrada xilka laga qaaday aysan luminayn shaqadooda guud ee dublamaasiyadeed, haddana waxaa lagu wargeliyay inay ku laaban karaan Washington si ay xilal kale uga qabtaan, haddii ay doortaan.
Go’aankan ayaa walaac ka abuuray qaar ka mid ah Mareykanka iyo ururka metela diblomaasiyiinta, kuwaas oo ka digay in isbeddelladan degdegga ah ay saameyn ku yeelan karaan xiriirka Mareykanka iyo dalalka ay khuseyso oo ay Soomaaliya ka mid tahay.

5. Saadaashu in aanay karin:

Hadafyada ugu waaweyn ee doqonku leeyahay waxa kamid ah, in uu noqdo mid aan la saadaalin karayn talaabada xigta ee uu qaadi karayo, weedha xigta ee afkiisa ka soo bixi karta, iyo waxyaallada xigta ee uu geysan doono. Si yoolashaas shanta ah loo xaqiijiyo, looguna toosnaado, waxa ay doqmuhu yaqleelleen dastuur ka kooban shan xeer oo ay waajib ku tahay dhamaantoodba in ay u hogaansamaan. Shantaas xeer waa kuwo; caddaan ah, loo siman yahay, ujeed leh, oo fudud. Waxaana ay kala yihiin sidan soo socota.

Shanta xeer ee doqonnimada:

1. Hadalka in aanad u meel dayin:

Qofka doqonka ah weedhiisu waa in ay ahaato mid aan maskaxda soo marin, haddii ay soo martayna waa in aan shaandho la soo marin. Haddii wax laga fiirsado waxa meesha ka baxaysa xurriyadda qofka doqonka, taas oo aan ahayn mid cuntamaysa, doqonku waa in uu isa siiyo xurriyad hadalkiisana iska yidhaahdo, cid u midh-tirin kartaana ma jirto! 2. Degdeg faro badan:
 
Iyada oo lagu xisaabtamayo in noloshu gaaban tahay oo kol uun laga dhamaaneyso, qofka doqonka ahi waa in aanu wakhtigiisa qaaliga ah ku lumin kaadsiimo, feejignaan iyo dulqaad aan macno lahayn. Doqonka waxa waajib ku ah in ficilladiisa uu degdegsiimo ku darro, in aanu aad uga fikirin waxa ka imanaya, iyo in falkiisu aad uga horeeyo fikirkiisa. Maxaa yeelay? 3. Muran ma-dhalays ah:

Sida saxda ah qofka doqonka ahi isaga ayaa toosan had iyo jeer, cidkasta oo aan la aragti ahayna waxa ay ka dhigan yihiin col ay tahay in la iska dhiciyo, iyada oo qodobkaas la tixraacayo; waxa waajib ku ah qofka doqonka ah in uu galo halgan iyo dedaal baaxad leh, isaga oo adeegsanaya hubka culus ee muranka. 4. Isla-qumannaan:

Aduunkan dad badan ayaa jooga oo cadow ku ah bulshada doqmaha, cadaawahaasi waxa uu noqon karayaa sokeeye, saaxiib, mid dan idinka dhexayso iyo mid markaas uun aad is barateen; dhamaantood waxa ay ka siman yihiin in ay weerar iyo duullaan ku hayaan qofka doqonka ah. Sidaa awgeed, waxa waajib ku ah doqonku in uu difaac adag xidho, talada kuwaasna uu ka feejignaado.

5. Dhufaannida damiirka iyo sariigasho la’aanta:

Waxa jira cod xun oo qofka ku dhex jira, kaas oo dhegaha ugu rida in uu waxyaabaha uu wado badh kamid ah ka baydho, waa dareen qariib ah oo kugu keenaya in aad dhawrsatid, dulqaadatid,
 
naxariisatid, dadka kale iska horeysiisid, dantaada ilawdid, iyo in aad nuglaatid; intaas iyo in kale oo badanba waa uu keenaa. Doqonka waxa waajib ku ah in uu damiirka qalajiyo, kana ilaaliyo in uu ka qoyo.

Mar haddii aynu isla soo fahannay xeerarka iyo yoollalka doqmaha, waxa dadka waajib ku ah in ay maaro u helaan, maaradaasina waxa ay ku soo uruuraysaa shan qodob, oo qodobada kalena hadhow ka sii farcamayaan. Waxaanay kala yihiin sidan soo socota.

Shanta xal ee doqonnimada:

Waxa xaqiiq ah haddii la doonayo arrin in maaro loo helo, waxa waajib ah in si waafi ah loo barto horta. Doqonnimada waa in la qeexo, la furfuro, waxna laga barto. Waa in doqonka la shey- baadho, xogtiisa la helo, dabeetana la isku dayo in la fahmo isna wax la fahansiiyo.
