But in May it was on camera and we had the footage, and, you know, no one wanted to have them on air…I’m not sourcing or quoting; I just saw with my eyes, and it was in the beginning of the revolution, it was just, like, one month and a half from the revolution…I was seeing a lot of weapons, people with RPGs, people with Kalashnikovs, you know, just crossing from the borders. And they were not one or two; they were a big number; they were just dominating the whole village that we were on the borders with. So, you know, the militarization of the revolution started early.”
Hashem later resigned from al-Jazeera to protest the channel’s refusal to broadcast his reports of armed militants crossing into Syria. He speculated that al-Jazeera’s editors were attempting obscure the violent nature of the uprising, as there were those who “wanted to say that al-Assad is facing the peaceful crackdown with weapons, while the others on the revolution side are kind of peaceful people, are not holding weapons.” This is unsurprising, given that al-Jazeera had been coordinating its news coverage with U.S. planners since at least 2010. Lebanese academic Asad Abu Khalil noted for example that “the head of al-Jazeera told me in 2010 that the US embassy in Doha Qatar sends a weekly report in which they provide a critique of every program that appears on al-Jazeera in order to have them change their tunes, to change it towards America.”
Hariri’s Holy War
Reporting from Der Spiegel suggests that the fighters witnessed crossing into Syria by Ali Hashem were Salafist militants from the Lebanese city of Tripoli. The German magazine reported that Sheikh Masen al-Mohammad, a prominent Salafist cleric in Tripoli, was sending fighters into Syria as early as summer 2011 because, in his view, “Assad is an infidel” and “There is a holy war in Syria and the young men there are conducting jihad. For blood, for honor, for freedom, for dignity.” According to one of the fighters interviewed by Der Spiegel, around 60 percent of the Lebanese fighters crossing the border from Tripoli to Homs had already fought in Iraq.”
These Salafist fighters included militants from an al-Qaeda affiliated group known as Fatah al-Islam. Dr. Haytham Mouzahem, director of the Beirut Center for Middle East Studies explained that, “When the uprising in Syria began in 2011, many of the remaining Fatah al-Islam members crossed the border and joined groups in the Free Syrian Army.”
Just as in Banias, the flow of arms and Salafist fighters into Homs was facilitated by Lebanese Prime Minister Saad Hariri, a close ally of both US and Saudi intelligence. Azmi Bishara noted that, “The circles close to the people who took up arms confirm that arms smuggling from Lebanon began in late April 2011” and that “The weapons were initially used for individual kidnappings or assassinations (in one day in the city of Homs in July, about 30 people were kidnapped and killed) while the public appearance of weapons in the streets began in August 2011. The armed battalions were formed in October 2011. Saad Hariri appears to have funded the smuggling of arms from Lebanon, as evidenced by the naming of some battalions by his name or by his father’s name.”
As discussed above, Hariri had partnered with Saudi intelligence to cultivate Salafist groups in Tripoli starting in 2005, including providing protection for militants from Fatah al-Islam in 2007. This was part of the “redirection” in U.S. policy in the region. U.S. planners had been battling Salafist militants in Iraq, including militants from al-Qaeda in Iraq, but pivoted to supporting such groups in response to growing fears about a so-called Shia Crescent.
Jisr al-Shagour
The above-mentioned al-Qaeda tactic of infiltrating demonstrations and attacking police stations was also evident in June 2011, in the northern Syrian town of Jisr al-Shagour.
As noted above, on June 3, 2011 tens of masked young men from the area of Jabal al-Zawiya in Idlib province arrived in Jisr al-Shagour on motorcycles with weapons they had purchased on the black market or had captured from government caches. These men were among those that attacked the pro-government Popular Army headquarters to capture additional weapons. Two days later, on June 5, Islamist militants attacked the local post office and military security headquarters, leading to a 36-hour gun battle.
According to journalist Rania Abouzeid, the violence began when an armed militant named Basil al-Masry was killed while attacking a government check point. Masry’s death angered many residents of the town, who believed rumors that Masry had been unarmed when he was killed, rather than carrying out an armed operation. As a result, his funeral doubled as an anti-government demonstration. As protestors approached the local post office, several hundred Islamist militants emerged from among the protestors and opened fire on government snipers stationed atop the post office roof. The militants then threw incendiary devices inside the post office doors, lighting the building on fire and burning eight people to death, before turning to attack the nearby military security building, where state security and political security personnel were holed up inside. When the Syrian authorities sent a convoy of soldiers to come to their assistance, the Islamist militants ambushed their convoy, killing some 120 of the soldiers.
Mass Graves, but Whose?
Opposition activists spread the false claim that the slain soldiers were defectors killed by their own Alawite superiors in the army, despite evidence to the contrary provided by Syria expert Joshua Landis, showing the soldiers had been killed by opposition gunmen. As Rania Abouzeid reported, it was only years later that activists involved in the incident acknowledged that the story of the soldiers defecting was fabricated. Abouzeid had herself reported on the incident at the time, and unwittingly passed on the false claims suggesting the dead soldiers had first defected. Abouzeid later reversed her reporting and provided full details of the event after interviewing an Islamist militant who had participated in the attack, as well as other civilians that were present in the initial protest outside the post office. The militant acknowledged to Abouzeid that he and his men had filmed the bodies of some of the security forces they killed and presented the videos as if they showed “mass grave’s full of the regime’s victims.” The fabricated claim about defecting soldiers was used to conceal the fact that the soldiers were killed by Islamist militants, and thereby allow the uprising to continue to be viewed as peaceful.
The militant quoted by Abouzeid, named Muhammad, had helped Islamist militants travel to Iraq to fight with al-Qaeda after the U.S. invasion in 2003. Muhammad’s brother had himself fought with al-Qaeda in Iraq leader Abu Musab al-Zarqawi in Falluja. Starting in 2009, Muhammad spent close to two years, off and on, in prison in Syria due to suspicions of his Salafist leanings, and was released without charge on January 11, 2011, shortly before the crisis erupted in March. He was detained again briefly for ten days on March 13, 2011 but released after signing a pledged to refrain from participating in anti-government activities. As discussed above, Mohammad quickly “enlisted a small group of Salafi friends from Latakia who, along with a few local men he’d armed, overran half a dozen small police stations in villages dotted around the city. The first raid was in mid-April, the same time as Jisr al-Shagour’s first protest.” After the attacks on Syrian security forces in Jisr al-Shagour in June 2011, Muhammad went on to become a commander in al-Qaeda’s official Syrian wing, Jabhat al-Nusra, or the Nusra Front.
Tending to the Necessary Details
Another Salafist militant who participated in the June 2011 ambush in Jisr al-Shagour, Hassan Aboud, had previous links to al-Qaeda as well.  Aboud had traveled to Iraq to fight against U.S. occupation forces in 2004 in Falluja and was seen in a video with al-Zarqawi. After returning to Syria in 2005, Aboud led an apparently unremarkable life as a mason and laborer, though locals from his hometown of Sarmin in Idlib province speculated he was sent back to Syria as part of an al-Qaeda sleeper cell.
Aboud participated in anti-government protests starting in March 2011, and then founded an armed group called Liwa Daoud as the opposition movement quickly became militarized. His brigade had expertise in using improvised explosive devices (IEDs), and Aboud later became a double amputee after an improvised rocket accidentally exploded near him.
C.J. Chivers of the New York Times writes that, “In June 2011, while Syrian protesters appealed for international support, Mr. Aboud participated in the ambush of an army convoy near Jisr al-Shoughour, four associates said.” Aboud’s friend, Daoud al-Sheikh, was killed in the fighting, leading Aboud to establish Liwa Daoud, or the Daoud Brigade, in his honor. “His brigade started small. But it set up a guerrilla base among olive groves and caves, where it trained, manufactured weapons, and extended its fight. By late 2011, it joined Suqour al-Sham, or Sham Falcons brigade…Many early rebel groups lacked experience, money, training, and cohesion. The Dawood Brigade was different, Mr. Aboud’s townspeople said. It tended to details necessary to become a fighting force.”
Saqour al-Sham, the FSA group of which Liwa Daoud became a part, was a Salafist militia and the strongest armed opposition group in Idlib for the first years of the conflict. Aboud became one of the most important military commanders in Saqour al-Sham after participating in several key battles against the Syrian army, including at the Taftanaz military airport, the Shabiba military base, the Air Defense College and the Madajin checkpoint Aleppo, the Jadida checkpoint in Hama, the Hamishu checkpoint in Idlib.
In 2014, Aboud defected with his fighters to ISIS, bringing with them weapons and a convoy of armored vehicles and tanks. Aboud became a prominent ISIS commander and led the ISIS assault on the Aleppo countryside in August 2014. He was known for threatening in songs to kill his former FSA counterparts. Aboud helped lead the attack to capture the ancient town and heritage site of Palmyra, after which ISIS publicly murdered Khalid al-Asaad, the retired director of antiquities for the site. Hassan Aboud was killed in March 2016 when his convoy struck a roadside bomb.
Six days after Salafist militants killed the 120 Syrian soldiers in Jisr al-Shagour in June 2011, Hala Jaber of the Sunday Times reported a similar incident, where Islamist gunmen used the cover of a demonstration to attack Syrian security forces, this time in the nearby town of Ma’arat al-Nu’man, also in Idlib province. According to tribal elders from the town, men armed with rifles and rocket propelled grenade launchers joined some 5,000 protestors demonstrating outside a military barracks in the middle of the town. The armed men attacked the barracks, where roughly 100 police were barricaded inside, causing a military helicopter to come to the aid of the police. Four policemen and 12 of the armed men were killed, while 20 policemen were wounded. The barracks was ransacked by a mob and set on fire, as was the local courthouse and police station.
Founding Of the FSA
In a rare admission of the armed nature of the fledgling anti-government uprising, Anthony Shadid of the New York Times reported on May 8, 2011 that, “American officials acknowledge that some protesters have been armed,” and that “Syrian television is suffused with images of soldiers’ burials.” By this time, at least 81 soldiers and police had been killed.
However, after the killing of the 120 Syrian soldiers in Jisr al-Shaqour in June 2011, cracks in the narrative of a peaceful uprising being crushed by a ruthless dictator were beginning to emerge. To reinforce the narrative that these soldiers were killed by their own officers after defecting, interviews were quickly arranged for journalists in the Western and Gulf press with Colonel Hussain Harmoush, who claimed to have defected from the Syrian army with thirty of his soldiers to protect civilians in Jisr al-Shagour after the alleged mutiny. These same outlets began airing YouTube videos of other alleged Syrian officers defecting to the opposition, including of colonel engineer Riad al-Asad, and Abd al-Razzaq Tlass, whose defection was deemed important because he is a relative of Manaf Tlass, the then-Brigadier General and childhood friend of Bashar al-Assad, and of Manaf’s father, Mustafa Tlass, the former Syrian Defense Minister and close advisor to Hafez al-Assad.
The publicity given to Harmoush, Tlass, al-Asad and other defectors paved the way for the establishment of the Free Syrian Army (FSA) on July 29, 2011. The establishment of the FSA provided cover public relations cover for a nascent Salafist-led insurgency that had already been active for months. The myth of a secular rebel army comprised of defected officers fighting to establish democracy and protect civilians was officially born.
Clear Sectarian Overtones
By August 2011, Homs had emerged as the epicenter of the conflict. The Salafist militants fighting in the city formally announced the founding of the Farouq Brigades, which began fighting under the FSA banner. One of the founders of Farouq, a lawyer named Abu Sayyeh, explained to journalist Rania Abouzeid that the group chose a name with “clear sectarian overtones tied to Assad’s alliance with Shiite Iran. The Farouq Battalions were named for Farouq Omar bin al-Khatab, a sahaba or companion of the prophet Muhammad, political architect of the caliphate and the second caliph who conquered the Sassanid Persian empire, among other territories. ‘We wanted to be called Farouq as an indication of our desire to confront Persian ambitions in our Arab lands,’ the lawyer Abu Sayyeh said.”
Walid al-Faris also notes the dominant role played by Salafists generally in the establishment of Farouq. He writes that “the biggest part of the financial support came from religious students of the Salafi methodology in Homs and outside it. This was confirmed by the announcement of the actual leadership of the brigade, which originally belonged to the Salafi methodology, and this was not apparent initially.” As mentioned above, the most important founder of the Farouq Brigades was a Salafi preacher named Amjad Bitar, who was able to fund the group via donations from Salafi networks in the Gulf states.
The Salafist orientation of the Farouq Brigade fighting in Homs was not apparent initially because the group was publicly led by a defected Syrian army officer, Abd al-Razzaq Tlass, who had defected from the Syrian army in June 2011 as mentioned above. Farouq also adopted the FSA brand, which gave it a secular veneer and allowed it to be presented as moderate in the Western press.
Al-Faris notes however that while Tlass handled military responsibilities, it was Bitar who was the actual leader of the group. After a trip to Syria in August 2012, opposition activist Ammar Abd al-Hamid similarly confirmed that although Farouq was apparently “run by a charismatic young defector, Captain Abdurrazzaq Tlas, it was guided from behind the scenes by a Salafi scholar by the name of Amjad Bitar.”
It was also commonly claimed that Farouq consisted primarily of army defectors who had refused to fire on peaceful civilian protestors. However, Farouq fighters consisted primarily of civilians from the Salafi community in Homs and/or militants from Fatah al-Islam who joined the group after crossing the border from Lebanon. Rania Abouzeid reports for example that “Opposition media activists pushed the idea that Farouq and the broader Free Syrian Army were largely comprised of defectors, but they were mainly armed civilians.” She quotes a Farouq commander named Abu Azzam as explaining that, “We are a civilian revolution, not a revolution of defected soldiers.”
McClatchy journalist David Enders spent time with a unit of Farouq fighters in April 2012. He notes that the group’s commander refused to say how many of his fighters were defectors, suggesting there were few, if any. Enders notes however that several fighters eagerly acknowledged to him that they had fought in Iraq against U.S. occupation forces, including in 2004 in Falluja, after Enders indicated he himself had reported from Fallujah at the time. Similarly, al-Jazeera journalist James Bays observed that the Farouq Brigades unit he was embedded with in al-Qusayr in May 2012, “includes many more civilian volunteers. Many don’t wear uniform, and some cover their faces with the keffiyeh, or arabic scarf. We were told some of these fighters had fought in Iraq.”
Despite the Salafist and explicitly sectarian orientation of Farouq, and its connections to al-Qaeda affiliated groups in both Lebanon and Iraq, Foreign Policy magazine would later describe the group as “at one point, the lynchpin of the West’s effort to build a ‘moderate’ opposition” in Syria.
Jolani Returns to Syria
In August 2011, after al-Qaeda elements had been already active in Syria for five months, Islamic State in Iraq (ISI) leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi dispatched his deputy Abu Muhammad al-Jolani from Iraq to formally extend the group’s franchise into Syria, which became known as the Nusra Front.
The Associate Press published a report providing an outline of Jolani’s life based on information from Iraqi and Jordanian intelligence and from a prominent Jordanian Salafi leader. The report explains that Jolani “was once a teacher of Arabic before moving to Iraq, where he turned to militancy and eventually became a close associate of Abu Musab al-Zarqawi, the Jordanian-born leader of the militant group al-Qaeda in Iraq. After al-Zarqawi was killed by a U.S. airstrike in 2006, al-Golani left Iraq, briefly staying in Lebanon, where he offered logistical support for the Jund al-Sham militant group, which follows al-Qaeda’s extremist ideology, the officials said. He returned to Iraq to continue fighting but was arrested by the U.S. military and held at Camp Bucca, a sprawling prison on Iraq’s southern border with Kuwait. At that camp, where the U.S. military held tens of thousands of suspected militants, he taught classical Arabic to other prisoners, according to the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were revealing information from secret files. After his release from prison in 2008, al-Golani resumed his militant work, this time alongside Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, the head of al-Qaeda in Iraq—also known as the Islamic State of Iraq. He was soon appointed head of al-Qaeda operations in Mosul province. Shortly after the Syrian uprising began, al-Golani moved into Syrian territory and, fully supported by al-Baghdadi, formed the Nusra Front, which was first announced in January 2012.”
These same details of Jolani’s life were confirmed by al-Jazeera in July 2015, and noted that al-Jolani returned to Syria from Mosul specifically in August 2011. Al-Jazeera is in a good position to know the outline of Jolani’s past, given that Jolani granted two major interviews to the network, one in December 2013 (Jolani’s first), and the other in 2015. These reports from the Associated Press and al-Jazeera contradict pro-opposition propaganda claiming that Jolani was held by the Syrian government in the prison at Sednaya, and deliberately released early in conflict to Islamize and militarize an otherwise peaceful and secular uprising.
Jolani’s presence in Syria remained secret, as did the role of foreign jihadists working with FSA groups during this period. For example, Aaron Zelin, an expert on Tunisian Jihadism, observed that, “In 2011, before jihadist groups officially announced their presence in Syria, foreign fighters began mobilizing to Syria with the non-jihadist Free Syrian Army…As for the announcement of foreign fighter martyrs, this began in February 2012, with the posting of the first recorded martyrdom notice on the jihadist forum Shamukh al-Islam. This announcement was long delayed, with the fighter in question, a Kuwaiti named Hussam al-Mutayri, having died August 29, 2011, while fighting with the FSA in Damascus.”
The announcement of the deaths of these foreign jihadists supporting the FSA was delayed until early 2012 because al-Qaeda had not yet formally announced its existence in Syria, though of course it had existed since the beginning of the conflict.
A Daily Diet of Suicide Bombings
Al-Qaeda first made its presence in the Syria conflict apparent with a suicide bombing in Damascus on December 23, 2011. Suicide car bombers targeted General Security Directorate and another branch of the security services, killing 44 including civilians and security personnel. Opposition activists claimed this was a false flag attack carried out by the government to discredit the armed opposition. However, Syria expert Joshua Landis cast doubt on this view, noting, “I am only surprised that we haven’t seen the use of suicide bombing sooner.” With the continued break down of law and order, radical groups would be able to spread and “the chances are that the daily diet of suicide bombings that have become a part of political life in Iraq, will also become common in Syria.”
As Landis expected, more such bombings quickly followed. According to Syrian state TV, a suicide bomber detonated explosives near a bus, killing some 26, including both civilians and security personnel in the Maidan district of Damascus on January 6, 2011. Opposition activists once again tried to claim the attack was a false flag carried out by the government.
Three weeks later, al-Qaeda made its role in the conflict public and explicit. On January 24, 2012, al-Jazeera reported that al-Jolani issued a “statement announcing the formation of the ‘Support Front for the People of the Levant’ whom he called ‘the Mujahideen of al-Sham,’ and took his homeland, ‘al-Shuhail’ as a starting point for the work of this front. In his statement, he also called on the Syrians to wage jihad and take up arms to bring down the Syrian regime.”
To the embarrassment of the U.S. and Gulf-backed political opposition, AFP reported that Nusra soon claimed responsibility for the Maidan attack, as well as another mass casualty suicide bombing in Aleppo that killed 28 on February 10, 2011, and that U.S. Director of National Intelligence James Clapper suggested that the attacks bore the hallmarks of al-Qaeda in Iraq and that militants from the group had infiltrated into Syria to join the fight against the government.
Clapper’s acknowledgement of al-Qaeda’s operations in Syria coincided with warnings from Iraqi security official Adnan al-Assadi that “a number of Iraqi jihadists went to Syria,” and that “weapons smuggling is still ongoing.” Al-Assadi explained that the prices of weapons in Mosul (the province’s capital) are higher now because they are being sent to the opposition in Syria,” including through a border crossing near Abu Kamal,” a town in Syria’s Deir al-Zour province on the Euphrates river and opposite the Iraqi town of al-Qaim.
Cradle of the War
Assadi’s statements point to the early importance of Deir al-Zour province, which quickly became the epicenter of al-Qaeda’s activities in Syria. Guardian journalist Leith Abdul-Ahad was one of the few journalists to visit the province, and in July 2012 he noted that “Al-Qaida has existed in this parched region of eastern Syria, where the desert and the tribes straddle the border with Iraq, for almost a decade. During the years of American occupation of Iraq, Deir el-Zour became the gateway through which thousands of foreign jihadis flooded to fight the holy war. Many senior insurgents took refuge from American and Iraqi government raids in the villages and deserts of Deir el-Zour…[The regime had] for years played a double game, allowing jihadis to filter across the borders to fight the Americans while at the same time keeping them tightly under control at home.” Abdul-Ahad writes that, “In the pre-revolutionary days when the regime was strong it would take a year to recruit someone to the secret cause of jihad,” but according to a Nusra fighter, who had himself fought in Iraq as a young man after 2003 and participated in early demonstrations against the Syrian government in 2011, “Now, thanks to God, we are working in the open and many people are joining in.”
Abu Muhammad al-Jolani’s hometown of al-Shuhail played a particularly important role, as noted in the announcement of the Nusra Front’s establishment. Abdul-Ahad also visited al-Shuhail and noted that the town “has become the de facto capital of al-Qaida in Deir el-Zour. More than 20 of its young men were killed in Iraq. In Shahail the al-Qaida fighters drive around in white SUVs with al-Qaida flags fluttering.”
As mentioned above, American journalist Theo Padnos, a fluent Arabic speaker who was held captive by Nusra for two years, including for ten months in al-Shuhail, also pointed to the importance of Deir al-Zour in the anti-government insurgency that erupted in 2011. According to the fighters, fellow prisoners, and civilians with which he managed to speak, the Syrian revolution was not about democracy or human rights, but about waging war against the Alawites from the Syrian government and establishing an Islamic state. Padnos writes that, “I suspect now that the true cradle of the war in Syria wasn’t Deraa, where the famous graffiti ‘The People Want the Fall of the Regime’ first appeared on a schoolyard wall, but rather the Euphrates River Valley, especially the eastern portions of it, downstream from Raqqa, where Syria’s oil and gas fields lie,” and that “I suspect I quizzed dozens if not hundreds of Deiris, as people from this region are known (after the provincial capital, Deir Ezzor)…As it happened, I did not encounter a single person in the eastern half of Syria who believed that peaceful demonstrators in Deraa—or mosque goers in the restive suburb of Duma or citizens anywhere else in the west—were the true fomenters of a rebellion in Syria. The true fomenters, in the opinion of my prison interviewees, were the men of the jihad.”
The full name of the group established by Jolani suggests that Nusra (which means “support”) was meant to provide aid and assistance the existing Salafist armed groups already fighting under the Free Syrian Army brand. Ghaith Abdul Ahed quoted a Nusra commander in the town of Muhassan in Deir al-Zour named Abu Khuder who explained that “his men are working closely with the military council that commands the Free Syrian Army brigades in the region. ‘We meet almost every day,’ he said. ‘We have clear instructions from our [al-Qaida] leadership that if the FSA need our help we should give it. We help them with IEDs and car bombs. Our main talent is in the bombing operations.”
An Open Secret
In early 2012, FSA groups were not only receiving assistance from al-Qaeda in the east of the country in Deir al-Zour, but also in the northwest, near the border with Turkey. The assistance came in the form of al-Qaeda affiliated militants from the Libyan Islamic Fighting Group (LIFG) as well as shipments of Libyan weapons facilitated by the CIA and British intelligence.
Seymour Hersh reports that the CIA was running a “rat line” to ship weapons from Libya (from government stockpiles captured after the fall of Qaddafi in September 2011) to opposition militants in northern Syria. Hersh reports that, “The rat line, authorized in early 2012, was used to funnel weapons and ammunition from Libya via southern Turkey and across the Syria border to the opposition. Many of those who ultimately received the weapons were jihadists, some of the affiliated with al-Qaida.” Hersh notes that according to a classified annex to the Senate Intelligence Committee report on the attack on the U.S. consulate in Benghazi, Libya, in September 2012, an “agreement was reached in early 2012 between the Obama and Erdogan administrations. It pertained to the rat line. By the terms of the agreement, funding came from Turkey, as well as Saudi Arabia and Qatar; the CIA with support of MI6, was responsible for getting arms from Gaddafi’s arsenals into Syria. A number of front companies were set up in Libya, some under the cover of Australian entities. Retired American soldiers, who didn’t always know who was really employing them, were hired to manage procurement and shipping. The operation was run by [CIA director] David Petraeus.”
Though Hersh reports the CIA and MI6 weapons shipments began in early 2012, they likely began earlier, in at least November 2011, when “volunteer” fighters from the NATO-backed interim Libyan government began traveling to Syria to fight with FSA groups. On November 29, 2011 al-Bawaba reported that “600 rebel fighters have already gone from Libya to Syria in order to support the Syrian opposition” and “that the Libyan rebels entered Syria through Turkey, to join ‘the free Syrian army’” and “that the door is still open to more volunteers in Libya in case they wish to fight.”
The most prominent Libyan commander to travel to Syria was Mehdi al-Herati, a Quran teacher with Irish citizenship who had previously fought against U.S. occupation forces in Iraq in 2003. Al-Herati traveled from Ireland to Libya in February 2011 to form the Tripoli Brigade along with LIFG founder Abd al-Hakim Belhaj. The Tripoli Brigade spearheaded the invasion of the Libyan capital in August 2011 under the cover of NATO bombs.
Belhaj and other former LIFG militants were in turn partnering with British intelligence during the conflict. Middle East Eye (MEE) reported that Foreign Office minister Alistair Burt acknowledged that the British government was in communication with Libyan insurgents during this period, and it was “likely that this included former members of Libyan Islamic Fighting Group.” MEE reports further that according to Salafist activist and former Guantanamo detainee Moaezzem Begg, the “British government’s use of and support for former members of the LIFG during the Libyan uprising was a ‘pretty open secret.’”
Mahdi al-Herati then traveled to Syria in October 2011, just two months after the fall of Qaddafi, under the pretext of providing humanitarian aid. After crossing the border from Turkey, Herati went to the Jabal a-Zawiya region of Idlib province and met with leaders from an al-Qaeda affiliated Salafist militia, Ahrar al-Sham. According to Herati, he was welcomed “as a brother.”
Herati founded his own brigade, Liwa al-Ummah, in April 2012. Foreign Policy (FP) notes that the Facebook page for Liwa al-Ummah promoted a “video clip of the late Abdullah Azzam, a Palestinian religious scholar who provided the theological underpinning for the jihad against the Soviets in Afghanistan in the 1980s, outlining when jihad becomes fard ayn, meaning an individual duty. A message bylined by Harati contains an invitation to ‘join the jihad in the land of al-Sham.’” FP noted further that Herati’s men were well armed, with 12.5 mm and 14.5 mm anti-aircraft guns, rocket-propelled grenades, and rifles including PKCs and M16s at their disposal. Herati was able to recruit fellow Irish nationals to fight in Syria due to his standing in Ireland’s Salafist community. One young Irish fighter admitted that his plan to come fight in Syria initially worried his family, but that “They respect and trust Sheikh Mahdi, so when they learned I was coming to join him here, they felt a little better.”
Herati claimed that the brigade was almost entirely Syrian but that he and fellow Libyans were providing “training and organization,” as well as “playing a combat role and providing our Syrian brothers with our experience of the Libyan revolution.
In 2013, Ibrahim al-Mazwagi, a Brit of Libyan descent, allegedly became the first British jihadist to die in the Syrian conflict. The Independent reported that “According to the Facebook page set up in his honour, the north Londoner had fought in Libya in 2011 before heading to fight alongside his ‘brothers in Syria last August,” and that “He took part of [sic] a major operation against the Assad regime forces yesterday and passed in the ensuing battles.” According to journalist Tam Hussein, Mazwagi had fought in Libya for Herati’s and Belhaj’s Tripoli Brigade.
In Syria, Mazwagi fought as part of a group known as Katibat al-Muhajireen, or the Emigrants Brigade which consisted of foreign fighters from various countries, including Abu Omar al-Shishani, a red-bearded ethnic Chechen who went on to become one of the most noted military commanders of the Islamic State. As a former member of the Georgian military, al-Shishani received training from U.S. special forces.
Muhammad Emzawi, another Londoner who later became a prominent member of the Islamic State, also fought for Katibat al-Muhajiroun after traveling to Syria in 2012. Known in the British press as “Jihadi John,” Emzawi gained notoriety after beheading journalists James Foley and Steven Sotloff, and aid workers David Haines, Alan Henning, and Peter Kassig, as well as 22 Syrian soldiers.
Shades of Bosnia
Emzawi and Mazwagi’s cases illustrate the role played by British intelligence in the pipeline that was established to facilitate the travel of British Jihadis to Syria. Journalist Nafeez Ahmed reports that according to former British counterterrorism intelligence officer Charles Shoebridge, the UK authorities “turned a blind eye to the travelling of its own jihadists to Syria, notwithstanding ample video etc. evidence of their crimes there,” because it “suited the US and UK’s anti-Assad foreign policy.” Ahmed notes this “terror-funnel is what enabled people like Emwazi to travel to Syria and join up with [the Islamic State] – despite being on an MI5 terror watch-list. He had been blocked by the security services from traveling to Kuwait in 2010: why not Syria?”
UK planners were once again relying on the jihadist networks they had built in London starting in the 1990’s. Hoos waxaa ku qoran taariikh kooban oo ku saabsan qaar ka mid ah hoggaamiyeyaashii halgamayaasha gumeystaha diidka ee Koonfurta Soomaaliya. Qaar ka mid ah xogta (sida taariikhda dhalashada ama dhimashada) si buuxda looma hayo diiwaanno sax ah, balse waxa la ogyahay doorkooda taariikheed.
1. Macallin Ibraahin Kabtoole
Dhashay: Qiyaastii dabayaaqadii qarnigii 19aad – Koonfurta Soomaaliya
Geeriyooday: Qarnigii 20aad horraantiisii (taariikh sax ah lama hayo)
Doorkiisa iyo dagaalladii uu hoggaamiyay:
Wuxuu ka mid ahaa culimadii iyo hoggaamiyeyaashii abaabulay kacdoonnada ka dhanka ahaa gumeysigii Talyaaniga.
Wuxuu hoggaamin jiray dagaallo ka dhacay gobollada Shabeellaha Hoose iyo Banaadir.
Waxaa lagu xasuustaa dhiirrigelinta jihaadka iyo wacyigelinta bulshada.
2. Sheekh Cabdi Gaafle
Dhashay: Qiyaastii 1850-meeyadii – Gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose (degaanka Biyamaal)
Dhimasho: 1922 (dagaal ayuu ku shahiiday)
Dagaallo taariikhi ah:
Hoggaamiyihii halgankii Biyamaal ee ka dhanka ahaa Talyaaniga.
Dagaallo culus oo ka dhacay agagaarka Marka iyo Shabeellaha Hoose (1908–1922).
Wuxuu caan ku ahaa adkaysi iyo abaabul beeleed mideysan.
3. Xaaji Weheliye 
Dhashay: Koonfurta Soomaaliya – qarnigii 19aad
Dhimasho: Qarnigii 20aad horraantiisii
Doorkiisa:
Ka mid ahaa hoggaamiyeyaasha abaabulay kacdoon ka dhan ah Talyaaniga.
Wuxuu taageeray dhaqdhaqaaqyada hubeysan ee gobollada Shabeellaha.
4. Cabdiraxmaan Faqi Abiikar
Dhashay: Koonfurta Soomaaliya – qarnigii 19aad
Dhimasho: Xog rasmi ah lama hayo
Taariikh kooban:
Wuxuu ahaa wadaad iyo halgamaa.
Ka qeyb qaatay dagaalladii diinta iyo gobannimada loogu diriray gumeysiga.
5. Macallin Muumin
Dhashay: Koonfurta Soomaaliya
Dhimasho: Lama hubo
Doorkiisa:
Ka mid ahaa culimadii iyo hoggaamiyeyaashii dagaalka ku hoggaamiyay bulshada.
Wuxuu door ka qaatay abaabulka iyo wacyigelinta halganka.
6. Jibriil Macalin Barrow
Dhashay: Gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose
Dhimasho: Qarnigii 20aad horraantiisii
Taariikh:
Ka mid ahaa hoggaamiyeyaasha deegaanka ee ka horyimid Talyaaniga.
Dagaallo ka dhacay agagaarka wabiga Shabeelle.

The National Academy of Maay Culture and Sciences, in collaboration with Hubaal Broadcasting Service, is honored to announce the premiere of a compelling documentary exploring the spiritual influence, cultural leadership, and enduring legacy of the highly venerated Aw Sheikh Ibdillow Isaag Moogaaw (Abdillow Isaagow)—a millenarian and catechetical poet, erudite Islamic scholar, and master of Arabic, Af-Maay, and Af-Garre (Karre). Renowned for pioneering an innovative pedagogical approach, Sheikh Ibdille translated and explained the Shari‘a from Arabic into local languages through eloquent poetic compositions rather than the conventional laqbo system, making Islamic knowledge accessible to broader communities. His works span Tawhiid (theology), Arkaan al-Islam (the Five Pillars of Islam), Arkaan al-Iman (the Pillars of Faith), Shari‘a, Islamic history, and Qur’anic narratives—poems that continue to be chanted collectively by children, women, youth, and elders alike. This documentary celebrates a towering intellectual and spiritual figure whose teachings remain central to community identity, cultural continuity, and collective memory.

Kāzas bija beigušās, šampanietis sprāga un konfeti pazuda, bet īstais haoss sākās mājās. 🏠💔 Man bija divdesmit divi gadi, es stāvēju pie altāra kopā ar Polu, atraitni trīsdesmitgadniekam, un viņa diviem bērniem — Mia, septiņi, un Džonu, pieci — man blakus. Viņš man apsolīja, ka es būšu “tā īstā”, ne tikai viņam, bet arī viņiem. Viņa ideja, viņš teica, bija, ka mēs kā ģimene dosim zvērestus.

Sākumā tas šķita maģiski. Es palīdzēju Miai sasiet kurpju šņores, lasīju Džonam gulētiešanas pasakas, un mēs visi kopā smējāmies. Bet, tiklīdz medusmēnesis beidzās, maģija izgaisa. Pols vakaros devās uz videospēļu spēlēm, sakot, ka viņš “ir pelnījis atpūsties”, jo viņš apmaksā rēķinus. Es strādāju pilnu slodzi. Bērni… viņi sekoja viņa piemēram.

Es kļuvu par “ļaunāko raganu”, disciplinētāju, to, kas gatavoja ēst, uzkopja un apmierināja katru prasību, kamēr viņš bija “jautrs tētis”, smejoties par haosu, ko es pārvaldīju. Viņi apvienojās bandā, ķircināja mani, bet joprojām gaidīja, ka es reaģēšu uz katru mazāko iegribu. 😔

Līdz pirmā gada beigām es zināju, ka kaut kas ir jāmaina. Es jutos iesprostota solījumos, vainas apziņā, ģimenē, kuru mīlēju, bet kura mani neredzēja. Divus gadus vēlāk es sapakoju savas mantas, atstāju zīmīti un aizgāju. Šķiršanās bija rūgta, bet vienkārša — mēs aizgājām ar to, ko bijām atnesuši.

Ir pagājuši sešpadsmit gadi. Es apprecējos atkārtoti. Man pašai piedzima bērni. Dzīve ritēja uz priekšu… līdz vienai pēcpusdienai mans telefons iezvanījās. Ekrānā parādījās ziņa no Mias. Man sažņaudzās krūtis. Tā bija tāda ziņa, kas liek raudāt, tāda, ko nekad negaidi, bet nekad neaizmirsīsi. ❤️

Brīdis, kas notika tālāk… ne es, ne Mia nekad negaidījām. Turpinājums pirmajā komentārā 👇👇👇

​Eedeymaha loo jeediyay Qoyska Farxiya Kabayare

​Dabcasar ayaa soo saaray muuqaallo isdaba joog ah oo uu eedeymo kulul ugu jeedinayo qoyska ay ka dhalatay fanaanada caanka ah ee Farxiya Kabayare. Inkasta oo uusan Dabcasar si faahfaahsan u kala saarin dambiyada uu u haysto, wuxuu tilmaamay in dadkaasi ay qayb ka yihiin kooxo is hortaagan mashaariicda horumarinta diinta Islaamka.

​Khilaafka Masaajidka iyo Minnesota
​Warka ayaa intaas ku daraya in Dabcasar uu dad badan oo Soomaaliyeed oo ku nool Minnesota ku eedeeyay inay carqalad ku yihiin dhisme Masaajid uu isagu hormuud ka ahaa.

​Dhibicda dhacdada: Dabcasar wuxuu sheegay in "loogu dhacay" arrimo la xiriira dhaqaalaha iyo maamulka masaajidka.
​Mawqifka Farxiya iyo Africom: Ilaa iyo hadda, fanaanada Farxiya Kabayare iyo fanaanada kale ee Africom kama aysan hadlin weerarkan afka ah, iyadoo aamusnaantooda dad badan ay siyaabo kala duwan u tarjunteen.

​Toobadii Dabcasar iyo Isbadalka Cusub
​Ninkan oo markii hore caan ku ahaa hadallo kulul iyo "Zlatan-nimo", ayaa dhowaan sheegay inuu toobad keenay. Wuxuu qirtay inuu ka qoomameynayo hadaladii hore ee aan anshaxa lahayn ee uu ku baahin jiray TikTok iyo Facebook Live.
​Hase yeeshee, dadka qaarkood ayaa rumeysan in wali qaabka uu u weeraro shaqsiyaadka caanka ah ay u muuqato mid ka fog dabeecadda toobada, halka taageerayaashiisuna ay u arkaan inuu "xaqa difaacayo".
​Dhaqanka "Fadeexadaha" ee Soomaalida Mareykanka

​Warbixintu waxay tilmaamaysaa in Soomaalida ku nool Mareykanka ay sanadihii u dambeeyay caado ka dhigteen:
​Is-ceebeynta: Isticmaalka TikTok si loogu baahiyo ceebaha gaarka ah.
​Dagaalka Tooska ah (Live): Halkaas oo lagu kala baxo marka ay is-qabtaan shaqsiyaadka caanka ah.

​Saamaynta Culimada: Inkasta oo culimadu ay horey u cambaareeyeen hab-dhaqankan, haddana saamaynta baraha bulshadu waxay ka xoog badatay taladii waayeelka.
​Ogeysiis: "Xaaladda ayaa u muuqata mid weji cusub yeelan doonta haddii ay dhinacyada kale ee la eedeeyay ay soo jawaabaan."

Xiisadda Sheekh Dabcasar & Qoyska Farxiya Kabayare – Falanqeyn
1) Asalka Muranka
Khilaafkan wuxuu ka bilowday muuqaallo uu soo saaray Sheekh Dabcasar oo uu eedeymo culus ugu jeediyay qoyska ay ka dhalatay Farxiya Kabayare. Eedeymuhu si faahfaahsan looma caddeyn, balse waxaa lagu xiray arrimo ku saabsan carqaladeynta mashaariic diini ah, gaar ahaan dhismaha masaajid la sheegay inuu hormuud ka ahaa.

Marka eedeyn noocan ah la soo bandhigo iyadoo aan la keenin caddeyn muuqata, waxay si degdeg ah u noqotaa arrin shaki iyo kala qaybsanaan dhalisa. Taasi waa meesha khilaafku ku sii kululaado.

Minnesota waa meel ay ku badan yihiin Soomaalida Mareykanka. Marka masaajid ama mashruuc diini ah la sheego in lagu muransan yahay, arrintu ma aha mid fudud.
Haddii run tahay in:
Khilaaf dhaqaale jiro
Is qabqabsi maamul jiro
Eedeymo lagu kala tuhmayo
Markaas arrinta saxda ah waa in lagu xalliyo:
Guddiyo dhexdhexaad ah
Caddeyn qoraal ah
Xisaab furan
Laakiin haddii baraha bulshada lagu qaado, waxay isu beddeshaa fadeexad dadweyne oo aan xal keenin.
3) Aamusnaanta Farxiya & Africom
Ilaa hadda Farxiya Kabayare iyo Africom si rasmi ah ugama hadlin.

Aamusnaanta waxaa loo fasiri karaa laba siyaabood:
Inay ka fogaadaan kor u qaadista muranka.
Inay sugayaan waqti ama talo sharci.
Si xeeladaysan, mararka qaar aamusnaantu waa ka awood badan tahay jawaab degdeg ah.

A Miskolci Járásbíróság elrendelte azoknak a gyanúsítottaknak a letartóztatását, akik a megalapozott gyanú szerint cigarettáért és pénzért erőszakoskodtak Mezőkövesden.
A rendelkezésre álló adatok szerint a gyanúsítottak 2026. február 10-én este Mezőkövesden leszólították a sértettet, hogy tőle cigarettát, és pénzt kérjenek. A sértettnél hagyományos cigaretta nem volt, így az elektromos cigarettáját nyújtotta oda a fiatalkorú gyanúsítottnak, aki a sértettet ekkor egy alkalommal bordatájékon rúgta. Ezt követően a fiatalkorú terhelt a sértettet több alkalommal testszerte megütötte, miközben pénzt követelt tőle. A bántalmazástól a sértett a földre került, ahol a két gyanúsított közösen 25-30 alkalommal megrúgta, illetve több alkalommal testszerte – de leginkább fejtájékon – ököllel is megütötte őt, miközben folyamatosan pénzt követeltek tőle.  
A földön fekvő sértett próbált védekezni és kérte a gyanúsítottakat, hogy fejezzék be a bántalmazását, melynek végül az vetett véget, hogy az egyik szemtanú is felszólította őket cselekményük abbahagyására, majd a sértett segítségére sietett. A terheltek végül a sértettől elvett elektromos cigarettával távoztak.
A sértett a bántalmazás következtében 8 napon belül gyógyuló sérüléseket szenvedett. A gyanúsítottak cselekménye – bizonyítottság esetén – alkalmas lehet társtettesként elkövetett rablás bűntettének és súlyos testi sértés bűntettének kísérlete megállapítására.
A bűncselekmények súlyos büntetési tételére figyelemmel fennáll a szökés, elrejtőzés veszélye, amit a terheltek személyi körülményei nem ellensúlyoznak. Tartani kell attól is, hogy szabadlábon hagyásuk esetén a sértett vagy más tanú befolyásolásával, megfélemlítésével meghiúsítanák, megnehezítenék a bizonyítást, illetve előéletük, életvitelük alapján alappal lehet következtetni a bűnismétlés lehetőségére is.
A bíróság mindezeket mérlegelve egy hónapra, 2026. március 13. napjáig elrendelte a gyanúsítottak letartóztatását. A végzés a fiatalkorú gyanúsított vonatkozásában végleges.

Dagaalkii Lafoole wuxuu dhacay 25–26 Nofeembar 1896.
Wuxuu ka dhacay deegaanka Lafoole, oo qiyaastii 12 mayl u jira xeebta Banaadir (meel u dhow Muqdisho).
2️⃣ Yaa hoggaaminayey?
Dhinaca Talyaaniga:
Waxaa hoggaaminayey Antonio Cecchi, oo ahaa sahamiye iyo wakiil Talyaani ah.
Waxaa la socday saraakiil Talyaani ah iyo askar (askaris).
Dhinaca Soomaalida:
Waxaa hoggaaminayey odayaal iyo dagaalyahanno ka tirsanaa beelaha deegaanka Banaadir, gaar ahaan:

1..wacdaan
2.Murusade
3.Abgaal
4.Galja’aal
5 Shikhaal
(Isbahaysi qabiillo ah oo ka hortagay gumaysiga)
3️⃣ Qasaaraha intee ayuu le’egaa?
Talyaaniga:
In ka badan 80 Talyaani iyo askari ayaa la dilay.
Cecchi laftiisa waa la dilay.
Waxaa badbaaday oo keliya 3 askari.
Soomaalida:
Qasaaraha saxda ah lama diiwaangelin, laakiin wuxuu ahaa mid aad uga yar kan Talyaaniga.
4️⃣ Guusha yaa raacday?
✅ Guushu waxay raacday ciidamada Soomaalida.
Weerarkii Talyaaniga si buuxda ayaa loo jebiyey, waxaana la hakiyey isku daygii ay ku geli lahaayeen gudaha Banaadir muddo dheer (illaa 1908).
5️⃣ Ciidamada meeqo ayay kala ahaayeen?
Talyaaniga:
Qiyaastii 70 askari (askaris)
16–20 Talyaani ah (saraakiil iyo shaqaale markab)

Tiro rasmi ah lama hayo, balse waxay ahaayeen boqolaal dagaalyahanno ah oo ka soo jeeday beelaha deegaanka.

ইমাম আবু হানিফা, মালেক, শাফেঈ, আহমাদ বিন হাম্বল কেউ কি বাধ্য করেছেন? 

কেউ কি ফরজ ওয়াজিব বলেছেন??

Ada Hadits Kanjeng nabi tentang keutamaan malu yang diriwayatkan dalam Shohih muslim 1/63 :

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عن النبي ﷺقال: «الإِيمَانُ بِضْعٌ وَسَبْعُونَ شُعْبَةً. وَالْحَيَاءُ شُعْبَةٌ مِنَ الإيمان».

Diriwayatkan dari Sahabat abi Hurairah Kanjeng nabi dawuh "Iman itu tujuh puluh lebih cabangnya, Dan malu salah satu cabang dari iman"

Imam An-nawawi menuqil dawuh para ulama terkait alasan malu sebagian dari iman dalam Syarah shohih muslim 2/5 :

وَقَالَ الْقَاضِي عِيَاضٌ وَغَيْرُهُ مِنَ الشُّرَّاحِ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ وَإِنْ كَانَ غَرِيزَةً لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ يَكُونُ تَخَلُّقًا وَاكْتِسَابًا كَسَائِرِ أَعْمَالِ الْبِرِّ وَقَدْ يَكُونُ غَرِيزَةً وَلَكِنَّ اسْتِعْمَالَهُ عَلَى قَانُونِ الشَّرْعِ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى اكْتِسَابٍ وَنِيَّةٍ وَعِلْمٍ فَهُوَ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ بِهَذَا

Imam Al-Qhodi iyad dan ulama yang lain menjelaskan diberbagai Kitab syarah "Sesungguhnya malu dijadikan bagian dari iman, walaupun malu adalah Naluri manusia. Alasannya karena malu bisa dibentuk dan diperoleh seperti amal kebaikan. Dan Mungkin juga malu adalah naluri yang beramal pada peraturan agama dan membutuhkan pada upaya, niat dan ilmu. Maka malu digolongkan bagian dari iman sebab penjelasan ini.

 وَلِكَوْنِهِ بَاعِثًا عَلَى أَفْعَالِ الْبِرِّ وَمَانِعًا مِنَ الْمَعَاصِي.

"Dan Karena Malu adalah salah satu sifat yang mendorong untuk melakukan kebaikan dan mencegah dari perbuatan maksiat".

FRONTIÈRE KENYA–SOMALIE : RUTO PREND LE RISQUE — RENAISSANCE ÉCONOMIQUE OU PORTE OUVERTE À AL-SHABAB ? 

Par KongoTimes!

Près de quinze ans après sa fermeture en octobre 2011, la frontière entre le Kenya et la Somalie s’apprête à rouvrir officiellement en avril, selon l’annonce du président kényan William Ruto. Cette décision marque un tournant stratégique dans les relations bilatérales et dans la gestion sécuritaire d’une région longtemps marquée par les attaques du groupe islamiste Al-Shabaab.

La frontière avait été fermée lorsque Nairobi avait lancé une offensive militaire majeure en Somalie pour repousser les combattants d’Al-Shabab, affiliés à Al-Qaïda, loin de ses zones frontalières. Les troupes kényanes avaient ensuite été intégrées à la mission de l’Union africaine en Somalie, toujours active aujourd’hui.

UNE MENACE QUI RESTE BIEN RÉELLE

La décision de rouvrir intervient pourtant dans un contexte sécuritaire fragile. Le groupe Al-Shabab a revendiqué plusieurs attaques meurtrières sur le sol kényan ces dernières années.

Parmi les plus marquantes :

- L’attaque du centre commercial Westgate à Nairobi en 2013 (67 morts).
- Le massacre de l’université de Garissa en 2015 (148 morts).
- L’assaut contre l’hôtel DusitD2 à Nairobi en 2019 (21 morts).
- L’exécution de 28 passagers d’un bus à Mandera en 2014.

Ces attentats ont profondément marqué l’opinion publique et justifié pendant des années la fermeture stricte de la frontière.

DES GARANTIES SÉCURITAIRES RENFORCÉES

Face aux inquiétudes, William Ruto a assuré qu’un important déploiement de forces de sécurité accompagnera la réouverture des postes frontaliers, notamment à Mandera, ville du nord-est kényan à forte population somalie.

L’objectif affiché est double :

1. Empêcher l’infiltration de combattants.
2. Lutter contre le trafic d’armes et la contrebande transfrontalière.

Le Kenya avait également lancé en 2015 la construction d’une barrière de sécurité le long des 680 km de frontière commune. Mais le projet avait été suspendu après seulement 10 km construits, pour un coût estimé à 35 millions de dollars.

UN PARI ÉCONOMIQUE ET SOCIAL

Au-delà de l’enjeu sécuritaire, Nairobi invoque une nécessité économique. La fermeture prolongée a isolé les communautés frontalières, notamment à Mandera, où les liens familiaux et commerciaux avec la Somalie restent étroits.

Ruto affirme que la réouverture doit stimuler le commerce transfrontalier et favoriser une prospérité partagée. Pour de nombreux commerçants locaux, la reprise des échanges pourrait revitaliser une économie régionale fragilisée par des années d’instabilité.

UNE ANALYSE INQUIÉTANTE DE LA SITUATION EN SOMALIE

Cependant, un récent rapport du think-tank basé à Mogadiscio, le Hiraal Institute, met en garde contre un regain de puissance d’Al-Shabab. Selon ce document, le groupe aurait reconquis une grande partie des territoires perdus lors de l’offensive gouvernementale somalienne de 2022.

L’analyste Mohamed Mubarak souligne que cette offensive, bien que spectaculaire, manquait de stratégie à long terme et a entraîné d’importantes désertions au sein des forces somaliennes. Avec un mandat gouvernemental proche de son échéance, les perspectives d’une nouvelle offensive d’envergure semblent limitées.

ENTRE NORMALISATION ET RISQUE CALCULÉ

La réouverture de la frontière kényano-somalienne apparaît ainsi comme un pari stratégique : relancer les échanges sans compromettre la sécurité nationale.

Nairobi mise sur un dispositif sécuritaire renforcé et sur la coopération communautaire pour contenir la menace. Mais la résilience d’Al-Shabab et l’instabilité persistante en Somalie rappellent que cette normalisation reste fragile.

Entre impératif économique et prudence sécuritaire, le Kenya tente d’équilibrer ouverture et vigilance dans une région où la stabilité demeure un défi permanent.

Bahalkii uu ku dhuumanayay wuxuu isu beddelay sanduuq bir ah oo culus oo dhex yaalla goob dagaal oo holcaysa.
Kadib waxaa yimid weerarkii, gantaal toos ah, firir soo dhex galay xarunta taliska.
Darawalkii wuu miir-daboolmay, qiiq ayaa buuxiyay qolka, hababkii ilaalintuna way fashilmeen.

Taangiga dushiisana, kabaha ayaa soo dhowaanayay.

Wuxuu sheegay markii uu arkay kabaha dagaalyahannada inuu ogaaday in wax walba dhamaadeen.

Xilligaas wuxuu wajahayay isla'eg: inuu dagaallamo oo dhinto, ama inuu is dhiibo oo uu helo fursad uu ku noolaado.
Dhallinyaradii ayaa ka soo jiiday taangiga, sawirkii bahdilka ahaana wuxuu u faafay sida dab caws qabsaday.
Ma ahayn kaliya qabasho askari, ee waxay ahayd soo koobid culus oo ku saabsan burburkii saacadihii hore.
​Waxa ugu yaabka badnaa sheekadiisa ma ahayn qabashadiisa, balse wixii ka dambeeyay.

Wuxuu ka sheekeeyay booqasho kedis ah oo ka dhacday dhexda godka (tunnel-ka).
Nin ay ilaalo adag hareereysan tahay ayaa soo galay, wuxuu fadhiyay ilaa toban daqiiqo, si deggan ayuu u hadlay, wuxuuna ka codsaday inay sugaan inta laga gaarayo waqtiga soo laabashadooda, bilowgii ma uusan garanayn cidda uu yahay.
Kadib faahfaahinta ayuu ka fahmay inuu hor taagan yahay hoggaamiye sare, waa Yaxya Sinwaar.
​Nimrod markii dambe wuxuu ku soo baxay heshiis is-dhaafsi.

Wuxuu sheegay in daqiiqaddii ugu adkayd noloshiisa ay ahayd markii uu ku jiray taangiga xumaaday, dab iyo qiiq dhexdooda, markii uu dareemay in wax walba dhamaadeen.

Wuxuu kaloo sheegay in ka soo bixitaankiisii Qaza ay ahayd lama filaan uusan fileyn kadib markii uu ka quustay inuu badbaado.
​Laakiin sheekadu halkan ma ahan sheeko askari kaliya...

Sheekadu waxay tahay in "Taangigii weynaa" uu xumaaday,
Iyo in "Goobtii si buuxda loo sugayay" ay ku dhacday saacado gudahood,

Iyo in "Ciidankii aan la jebin karin" uu is dhiibay isagoon wax iska caabin ah sameyn,
Iyo in hal sawir uu ku filnaa inuu burburiyo sheeko dhan oo ku saabsan awoodda iyo xakamaynta buuxda.

Taariikhda mararka qaar laguma qoro bayaannada ciidamada, balse waxaa lagu qoraa daqiiqad naxdin leh,

Iyo sawir u faafa si ka dheereysa rasaasta.

Tiirka 1-aad: Maamulka iyo Hoggaanka (Governance) – Dib-u-habeyn iyo xoojinta nidaamka hoggaamineed.
Tiirka 2-aad: Tayada Daryeelka (Clinical Excellence) – Kor u qaadista tayada adeegyada caafimaad iyo badbaadada bukaanada.
Tiirka 3-aad: Kobaca Adeegga iyo Xogta (Data & Growth) – Horumarinta nidaamka xog ururinta iyo ballaarinta adeegyada.
Tiirka 4-aad: Aqoonsiga Shaqaalaha (Recognition) – Dhiirrigelinta iyo abaalmarinta shaqaalaha dadaalka muujiyay.
 
Sidoo kale, maamulka sare ee isbitaalka ayaa gudoonsiiyay shahaado sharaf shaqaalaha qeybta IPD iyo madax-qeybeed ka ugu wanaagsanaa muddadii 100-ka maalmood, taas oo ka tarjumeysa dadaalkooda, daacadnimadooda iyo doorka muuqda ee ay ku leeyihiin badbaadinta iyo daryeelka bukaanada jiifa isbitaalka.
 
Ugu dambeyn, Xoghayaha Joogtada ayaa si gaar ah u bogaadiyay waxqabadka muuqda ee isbitaalka, isaga oo ballan qaaday in shaqaalaha la siin doono xuquuqda u qalanta iyo fursadaha waxbarasho ee ay mudan yihiin, si loo sii xoojiyo adeegyada ay u hayaan bulshada iyo ciidamada.

Selama tiga setengah dekad, Jabatan Amal Malaysia bukan sahaja membina kekuatan fizikal dan kepakaran operasi, bahkan memperkukuh asas doktrin, disiplin dan sistem latihan agar setiap gerak kerja berteraskan prinsip Islam, kepatuhan organisasi dan kepentingan masyarakat.

Semoga ulang tahun ini menjadi titik lonjakan baharu untuk memperkemaskan modul latihan, memperluas penyelidikan (R&D), serta melahirkan generasi anggota yang lebih berilmu, berkemahiran dan berakhlak tinggi.

Ujeeddada tababarku waxay ahayd in la xoojiyo habraacyada amniga ee lagu shaqeeyo marka ay ciidanku ku jiraan hawlgallada dab-damiska, gaar ahaan xaaladaha ay ka dhalan karto nabadgelyo darro sida dhagax-tuurka lagu sameeyo ciidanka marka ay gudanayaan waajibaadkooda badbaadinta naf iyo maal. Intii uu socday tababarku, waxa si qoto dheer loo falanqeeyey khataraha jira iyo sidii looga hortagi lahaa falalka carqaladaynaya shaqada gurmadka.

Tababarka waxa sidoo kale qayb libaax leh ka qaatay madaxda Guddiyada Nabadgelyada ee sagaalka degmo ee caasimadda, maadaama arrintani si toos ah u saamaynayso degmooyinka iyo bulshada ku dhaqan. Qodobada muhiimka ah ee tababarka lagu lafaguray waxa ka mid ahaa:

•Hababka ugu habboon ee lagu sugi karo ammaanka goobaha dabku ka kaco.
•Sida loo maareeyo xaaladaha kacsan iyada oo aan la carqaladayn hawsha gurmadka.
•Doorka degmooyinka iyo guddiyada nabadgelyadu ku leeyihiin ka hortagga falalka khatarta ah.
•Xoojinta wada-xiriirka degdegga ah ee u dhexeeya ciidanka dab-damiska, Dawladda Hoose iyo bulshada.

SOONQAADSAN

Waxaa berri curanaysa bishii soonqaad (2026 | 1447), ee bilaha dayax muslimeedka ugu sedka badneed, oo qof walba oo awooda laga rabo, in uu ka afhaysto biyaha, cuntada, galmada iyo xumaha oo dhan. 

Waa maalmo suubban, bil barakaysan iyo toddobaadyo towbo, marka anaga oo fursaddan ka faa’iidaysanayna, ayaan idin leenahay; anagoo bahda xaruntu Shuuriye ah dhammaanteen: SOONQAADSAN. 

Ka dib, suugaantu waa tebin dareen, aqoon, ogaal ama aqool, oo wacyigelin iyo waano nololeed xambaarsan. Waa nuxurka aragtiyo, milicsiyo iyo maamin kuwooda ugu tayada badan.

Dad badan ayaa mooda, in ay tahay keliya jecayl-tebin iyo libin dagaal ku geeraarid, haddana, marar badan waxaad helaysaa, suugaan ka xeeldheer kumannaan wadaad wacdigood, sida warkeedu u kooban yahay, haddana ay u qotodheer tahay dareen, tilmaam iyo hugotusba. 

Marka waxaan jecelnahay, in aan idin la wdaagno meerisyo ka mid ah suugaantii abwaan Faarax Shuuriye, ee ku aaddaneyd soonka, salaadda iyo samo aqooneedka diineed. 

Geeraarkii caanka ahaa, ee “Ma is raaci karaan?” Wuxuu abwaan Faarax Shuuriye ku lahaa:

“Nin Salaadda rumeeyoo
Ruknigeeda yaqaanoo
Rukuucda iyo Sujuudda
Rabbigay u la jeediyo
Kub-caddaaga riddoobey
Ma is raaci karaan?
Nin masaajid ku raagoo
Cilmi raatib yaqaanoo
Wardigiisa ridaayiyo
Rufiyaanno dulloobay
Ma is raaci karaan?

Rammadaan ninka soomoo
Soddonkii iska reeboo
Maalintii rudhmo diidiyo
Nin makhaayadda ruugoo
Hadba rooti ka qaadan
Ma is raaci karaan?”.

Mar kale, abwaan Faarax wuxuu ku yiri gabaygii “Bulacle”: 

“Mowlaca salaad loo dhisiyo, guri masaajiidda
Iyo munkarka meel lagu tumaa, kala maqaan weyne.”

Mar kale, abwaan Faarax wuxuu gabay ku yiri:

“Nin cilmiga ku raagee bartana, xaqa hadduu raadsho
Ra’yi gaabtu wey uga hartaa, rubacyaleydaaye”

Mar kale dhammaantiin, dhammaanteen waxaan idin leenahay; soonqaadsan, waxaanna idiin quuddarraynaynaa, in aad ayaamahan ku qaadataan sinnaan iyo samaan. Soon aqbalan, ajar badan iyo afur macaan.

Maamulka iyo bahda Xarunta Dhaqanka iyo Suugaanta Faarax Shuuriye

Wiilkaygiiyow, aniga oo ku hadlaya faan iyo farxad weyn ayaan kuu sheegi karaa in ku koritaanka Somaliland uu ahaa mid ay ka buuxaan madadaalo iyo xiiso, bisha ugu xiisaha badnayd oo dhan waxa ay ahayd Ramadaan. Tuuladayada Dilla ee gobolka Awdal, halkaas oo aan ku soo barbaaray, iyo tuulo kasta oo Somaliland ka mid ah, xiisuhu wuxu bilaaban jiray fiidkii maalinta koowaad ee Ramadaanta. Dadka oo dhan waxaa ka buuxay rabitaan iyo rajo ah inay noqdaan kuwii ugu horreeyay ee arka bilaha cusub, sidaas darteed dadka tuuladu waxay u yaaci jireen meelaha bannaan iyo buuraha ku yaalla duleedka si ay uga qayb qaataan raadinta bisha Ramadaan...

Habeennada Ramadaantu waxay lahaayeen dareen u eeg bandhigyada muusigga casriga ah ee maanta. Dadweyne tiro badan ayaa isugu iman jiray maqaayadaha shaaha, iyagoo safaf is garab fadhiya dusha  dermo caws ah, dhammaantoodna qayilaya, cabbaya shaah madow oo khafiif ah oo macaan, isla markaana mararka qaarkood shidaya foox ku jira shoolad yar oo la yiraahdo girgire, taas oo si xeeladaysan meelo kala duwan loogu dhigi jiray si ay goobta u diiriso una fududeyso in saamaynta qaadku si degdeg ah u bilaabato.
Xiddigaha Rock and Roll-ka ee habeennada Ramadaantu wax ay ahaayeen wadaaddada, kuwaas oo si yaab leh u soo jiidan jiray dhegeystayaasha iyaga oo ku luuqaynaya heeso diini ah oo Carabi ah – af ay Soomaalidu u qaddarin jireen in uu yahay kan ugu barakaysan dunida, maadaama Ilaaha Qaadirka ahi u doortay inuu ku hadlo, isla markaana ay aaminsanaayeen in Carabigu yahay afka ay dhammaan dadku ku hadli doonaan marka ay aakhiro tagaan. Sidaas darteed marka wadaadku ku dhawaaqo tuduca koowaad, mowjad xasuus iyo hilow leh ayaa qabata dadkii, durbaanka iyo sacabka la socda ayaana dhammaantood gaarsiiya heerka ugu sarreeya ee raynraynta ruuxiga ah.

Habeennada Ramadaanta iyo maalmaha Ciidda waxay ahaayeen munaasabado farxad leh oo ay diinta iyo dhaqanka deegaanku isku biireen si ay u abuuraan dhaqan Soomaaliyeed Islaami ah oo qurux badan oo farxad leh. Kuwaas shisheeyaha ah waxay u rogeen dabaaldegyadeennii Ramadaanta iyo Ciidda munaasabado aan naf iyo ruux lahayn, aan muusig lahayn, aan halabuur lahayn. DAGAAL SOKEEYE OO LAGA DHIGAY MID ARGAGAXISO CAALAMI AH.

Dalalka Afghanistaan iyo Ciraaq oo ay ka jireen dagaaĺlo sokeeye u  dhaxeeyey bulshooyinkii ku noolaa dalalkaas, kuwaasoo loo sababay  arrimmo siyaasadeed, mid bulsho iyo dhaqaale.
11 September 2001 dagaaladoodii ee sokeeye waxay isu bedeshay dagaal caalamka uga soo  horjeeddo ka hortagga argagixisadda isaga gudba qaaradaha (  international terrorism ).
Somalia waxaa dagaalkeeddii ee sokeeye si rasmi ah isagu bedelay mid argagaxiso  markii midowga maxkamadaha islaamka gacanta ku dhigeen Caasimaddii  dalka iyo ku dhawaaqidooddii jihaad ka dhan ah ciidamadda Ethiopia ( 2006 ).

Ku dhawaaqidii jihaadka oo loo fasiray iney aheyd in dalka Somalia  noqdo meel gabood iyo xarun abaabul u ah dhammaan ururadda islaamiga ee  xukun doonka ah. 
Dhinaca kalena, waxaa dad badani aaminsan yihiin;  la dagaallanka argagixisnimadda inuu bedelay dagaalkii qaboobaa ( cold  war ) ee ka dhexeyn jiray is gaashaanbuursigii ( Nato & Warsaw ) ee  leysu adeegsan jiray awr kiraaleyaal dagaal ( proxy war ).

Dariiqa ama wadadda waa dheer tahay oo waxaa weli jidka ku soo jira   dalalka Syrië, Libië, Sudan iyo Yemen oo weli ku dhex jira mowjadaha  dagaalladda sokeeye.
Waxaa la yiri; guud ahaan shucuubta  muslimiinta, gaar ahaan ummadda Somalida waa dad wax akhriyo (أمة  الاقراء) laakin aan waxba garanin ama fahmin Siyaasadda. 
Sidaas si la mid ah siyaasadda waa jecel nahay oo waa akhrinaa, laakin ma fahamno mana garanno biyo shubkeedda ( no comprehension ).

Diriwayatkan dari Sahabat abi Hurairah Kanjeng nabi dawuh "Iman itu tujuh puluh lebih cabangnya, Dan malu salah satu cabang dari iman"

Imam An-nawawi menuqil dawuh para ulama terkait alasan malu sebagian dari iman dalam Syarah shohih muslim 2/5 :

وَقَالَ الْقَاضِي عِيَاضٌ وَغَيْرُهُ مِنَ الشُّرَّاحِ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ وَإِنْ كَانَ غَرِيزَةً لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ يَكُونُ تَخَلُّقًا وَاكْتِسَابًا كَسَائِرِ أَعْمَالِ الْبِرِّ وَقَدْ يَكُونُ غَرِيزَةً وَلَكِنَّ اسْتِعْمَالَهُ عَلَى قَانُونِ الشَّرْعِ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى اكْتِسَابٍ وَنِيَّةٍ وَعِلْمٍ فَهُوَ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ بِهَذَا

Imam Al-Qhodi iyad dan ulama yang lain menjelaskan diberbagai Kitab syarah "Sesungguhnya malu dijadikan bagian dari iman, walaupun malu adalah Naluri manusia. Alhamdulillāh, the special Tajweed class conducted by 𝐒𝐀𝐖𝐓 𝐀𝐒𝐇‑𝐒𝐇𝐀𝐁𝐀𝐁 was successfully held on 16 February 2026 at the CIAS Room. This meaningful session was facilitated by 𝐇𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐞 𝐊. 𝐀𝐫𝐚𝐥, an officer of 𝐒𝐀𝐖𝐓 𝐀𝐒𝐇‑𝐒𝐇𝐀𝐁𝐀𝐁, and focused on important rules for the proper recitation of the Qur’ān.

During the session, the lecturer explained 𝐀𝐥‑𝐈𝐤𝐡𝐟𝐚̄’ (الإخفاء), which linguistically means “concealment.” In Tajweed, it refers to pronouncing the noon sākinah or tanween in a way that is between al‑Izḥār and al‑Idghām, without shaddah, while maintaining the ghunnah. This rule applies when noon sākinah or tanween is followed by one of the fifteen letters of Ikhfā’, so the sound is partially concealed while the nasal tone remains clear.

The session also covered 𝐀ḥ𝐤𝐚̂𝐦 𝐚𝐥‑𝐌𝐢̂𝐦 𝐚𝐬‑𝐒𝐚̂𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐡, which governs the pronunciation of the letter mīm when it carries a sukūn. Al‑Ikhfā’ ash‑Shafawī occurs when a sākinah mīm is followed by ب, causing the mīm to be hidden with ghunnah. Al‑Idghām ash‑Shafawī occurs when a sākinah mīm is followed by another م, causing the first mīm to merge with the second while keeping the ghunnah. Al‑Izḥār ash‑Shafawī occurs when the sākinah mīm is followed by any letter other than ب or م, in which case the mīm is pronounced clearly, especially before ف and و.

Beyond his words, The lecturer reminded everyone that mastering Tajweed requires consistency, patience, and a sincere intention for the sake of Allāh, showing that learning Qur’ānic recitation is a noble effort.

May Allāh accept this effort, reward the instructor and organizers, place barakah in the knowledge gained, and grant us the ability to apply what we have learned in our recitation and daily life.

Jazākumullāhu khayran wa bārakallāhu fīkum

SEMOGA SOLAT KITA DALAM BULAN RAMADHAN INI SEMAKIN MENEPATI SUNNAH

KECELARUAN BERAGAMA AKIBAT MENGAMALKAN HADITH TANPA PANDUAN FUQAHĀʾ

Terdapat segelintir yang menganggap apabila dia amalkan hadith maka itulah sunnah. Sedangkan hakikatnya, praktik sunnah bukan semudah itu sebaliknya hendaklah dia ikut panduan para ulama muktabar untuk mengetahui kefahaman yang sahih dan praktik sunnah yang sebenar dalam beragama.

Perbincangan tersebut saya telah huraikan panjang lebar dalam tiga artikel di bawah:

https://www.facebook.com/share/p/17xSug9xjx/

https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1BFUgpege2/

https://www.facebook.com/share/p/14cg64FAcAc/

Antara akibat dari amal hadith tanpa panduan ulama fiqh ialah ketikamana masuk ke dalam masjid atau surau, seringkali saya ternampak segelintir individu yang sembahyang berjemaah dalam keadaan kakinya betul-betul rapat dilekatkan pada kaki orang yang berada di sebelahnya sehingga kakinya agak terkangkang besar kerana dia ingin memastikan kedua-dua kakinya menyentuh kaki orang yang berada di sebelah kanan dan kirinya. Seperkara lagi yang saya perhatikan, orang yang sama ini sembahyang dengan meletakkan kedua-dua tangannya betul-betul di atas dadanya.

Persoalannya, mengapa dia sembahyang dengan sedemikian rupa? Jika dia mempunyai masalah dengan kaki atau tangannya sehingga terpaksa mengangkang kakinya dan terpaksa menaikkan tangannya  ke dadanya, maka hal itu tidak mengapa dan tidak menjadi masalah. Setiap kali saya melihat orang yang solat seperti itu, supaya tidak bersangka buruk, saya akan beranggapan bahawa kemungkinan dia ada masalah sendi pada tangan dan kakinya sehingga dia terpaksa solat dengan sedemikian rupa atau dia hanya mengikut-ngikut orang lain tanpa mengetahui duduk perkara yang sebenar. 

Namun untuk orang yang melakukan sedemikian, dia hendaklah bermuhasabah dan bertanya kepada dirinya sendiri adakah dia melakukan hal  itu kerana mendakwa ianya sunnah atau kerana ia berdasarkan hadith semata-mata, jika sedemikian itu anggapannya, maka ia menjadi suatu kemusykilan kerana tidak ada siapa dari ulama muktabar yang menyatakan sunnah untuk menunaikan solat dengan cara sedemikian rupa. Bahkan semua mazhab menyatakan bahawa makruh hukumnya meletakkan tangan naik ke paras dadanya.  

Berkenaan cara meletakkan tangan ketika solat adalah seperti berikut:

Mazhab al-Shafi’i: Meletakkan di atas pusatnya iaitu antara pusat dan dada. Baik untuk lelaki dan perempuan. 

Mazhab al-Hanbali: Pendapat pertama ialah meletakkan tangan di bawah pusat. Pendapat kedua ialah ialah di atas pusat. Pendapat ketiga ialah dibawah dada. Adapun meletakkan tangan di atas dada adalah makruh menurut Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal.

Mazhab al-Maliki: Pendapat pertama ialah melepaskan tangan ke bawah (irsal). Pendapat kedua ialah meletakkan di atas pusat.

Mazhab al-Hanafi: meletakkan tangan dibawah pusat untuk lelaki dan meletakkan di atas dada untuk perempuan.

Hadith dalam bab ini ialah: “Dari Wa’il, beliau berkata: Lalu  RasuluLlah SAW meletakkan tangan kanannya di atas tangan kirinya di atas dadanya (على صدره)”. (Riwayat Ibn Khuzaymah) 

Namun Imam Ibnu Hajar al-Asqalani menyatakan hadith ini da’if. Kerana dalam riwayat ada Mu’ammil bin Isma’il al-Basri dan ramai Muhaddithin mengatakan bahawa kalimah “…di atas dadanya” (على صدره) adalah penambahan (ziyadah) dari perawi. Sedangkan hukum-hakam tidak terbina di atas hadith da'if yang ditolak oleh para fuqaha'. Oleh kerana itu, kita dapati tiada seorang pun Imam Mazhab yang beramal dengan hadith ini secara literal. 

Adapun menurut Imam Abu Hanifah, wanita meletakkan tangannya di atas dadanya bukan beristidlalkan hadith  Sahih Ibni Khuzaymah ini, tapi beristidlalkan qiyas bahawasanya ia lebih menunjukkan sifat haya’ bagi wanita.

Oleh yang demikian, seseorang yang meletakkan kedua tangannya di atas dadanya sebenarnya tidak mengikut mana-mana tafsiran Ulama dalam memahami hadith sifat solat, bahkan makruh disisi Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, sebaliknya perbuatannya itu adalah mengikut pendapat Mazhab Hanafi secara qiyas untuk wanita. Adapun untuk lelaki, semua mazhab menyatakan bahawa kedudukan tangan adalah di bawah dada. 

Berkenaan kedudukan kaki ketika dalam saf, diriwayatkan dalam Sahih al-Bukhari sebagaimana berikut:

أقِيموا صفوفَكم، ثلاثًا، واللهِ لَتُقِيمُنَّ صفوفَكم أو ليُخالِفَنَّ اللهُ بينَ قلوبِكم، قال: فرأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ يُلزِقُ مَنكِبَه بمَنكِبِ صاحبِه، ورُكبَتَه برُكبَةِ صاحبِه، وكعبَه بكعبِه

Baginda SAW berkata: Luruskan saf kalian (tiga kali), demi Allah, kalian sama ada benar-benar meluruskan saf-saf kalian atau Allah akan cerai-beraikan hati-hati kalian. Maka aku (Nu’man bin Bashir) melihat lelaki merapatkan bahunya disebelah bahu orang disebelahnya, lututnya pada lutut orang disebelahnya, buku lalinya pada buku lali orang disebelahnya”.

Berkenaan hadith di atas, al-Hafiz Ibnu Hajar Al-Asqalani berkomentar dalam Fath al-Bari, beliau berkata:

قال الحافظ في ( الفتح ) : المراد بذلك المبالغة في تسوية الصفوف و تقاربها اهـ لاحقيقة الإلتصاق و يمكن أن أحدهم يمس منكبه منكب الآخر، فأما القدم و الركبة فلا يلزم التماس، و ذلك لأن البعض قد يتأذى من التلاصق و التقارب الشديد

“Maksudnya bersungguh-sungguh di dalam meluruskan saf bukan maksudnya betul-betul melekatkan. Boleh saja salah seorang mereka menempelkan bahunya ke bahu orang lain, adapun buku lali dan lutut tidak dilazimkan untuk saling bersentuhan. Yang seperti itu kerana terkadang seseorang merasa terganggu kerana tempelan dan desakan yang menganggu ini. Akan tetapi maksudnya ialah menegakkan barisan saf secara selari dan mengisi celah diantara saf hingga syaitan tidak boleh keluar masuk”.

Kenyataan yang dibuat oleh Imam Ibnu Hajar al-Asqalani di atas adalah pengamalan seluruh mazhab, tiada satu pun menyalahinya. Seseorang yang solat dengan mengangkangkan kakinya agar bersentuhan rapat dengan orang disebelahnya, adalah sebenarnya tidak mengikut mana-mana tafsiran Ulama Muktabar dalam memahami hadith mengenai saf solat.

Dia akan terjebak dengan makna zahir hadith tersebut kerana jika dia mendakwa perbuatannya itu adalah untuk mengikut hadith sahih tersebut, maka dia perlu tahu bahawa hadith sahih itu tidak hanya menyebut bahu bertemu bahu dan kaki bertemu kaki, akan tetapi juga menyebut buku lali bertemu buku lali dan lutut bertemu lutut, sedangkan untuk mengamalkannya secara literal adalah hampir mustahil.

Pada asalnya, saya menyangka bahawa pendapat melekatkan kaki dengan kaki ini adalah pandangan dari Ulama Salafi, namun sepanjang pencarian saya, ternyata semua tokoh Salafi bersetuju bahawa makna hadith kaki bertemu kaki bukan bersentuhan melekat.

Seorang tokoh Salafi, Shaykh Muhammad Bin Uthaymin mengatakan bahawa yang sunnah dalam bab ini ialah seseorang pada awal solat hendaklah merapatkan saf dan meluruskan barisan agar tiada orang yang kakinya maju ke hadapan dan orang lain mundur dibelakang. Beliau menjelaskan bahawa bukan sunnah untuk menyentuh jari kaki dengan orang disebelahnya sehingga dia melebarkan bukaan kakinya apabila orang disebelahnya menarik kakinya ke arah bertentangan. Bahkan ia bertentangan dengan sunnah kerana yang sepatutya ialah dia perlu memberi kelonggaran kepada jirannya dan tidak menganggunya dengan sentuhan kakinya yang rapat. Bahkan menurut beliau, perbuatan tersebut adalah bertentangan dengan sunnah.

Manakala ilmuan Salafi yang lain bernama Shaykh Salih Fawzan pula berpendapat hadith sahih di atas adalah bermaksud المحاذات  iaitu barisan saf yang selari bukan melekatkan kaki bersentuhan dengan kaki orang disebelahnya. Shaykh Bin Baz juga mengatakan bahawa maksud hadith diatas adalah memenuhkan saf dan selarikan barisan saf, bukan menempelkan kaki dengan kaki orang sebelah. Kenyataan semua tokoh Salafi dalam bab ini adalah sejajar dengan apa yang dijelaskan oleh para Ulama Muktabar yang lain.

Oleh yang demikian, seseorang yang solat berjemaah dengan mengangkang kakinya agar dapat bersentuhan dengan kaki orang disebelahnya dengan alasan untuk ikut sunnah, hendaklah dia mengetahui bahawa tiada seorang Ulama pun yang memahami sunnah dari hadith sifat saf dengan sedemikian rupa.

Seluruh perbincangan di atas membuktikan bahawa persoalan cara letak tangan dan cara merapatkan saf dalam solat sahaja sudah mencukupi untuk menunjukkan betapa pentingnya untuk seseorang yang ingin mengamalkan sunnah tidak hanya bergantung kepada teks hadith semata-mata, akan tetapi perlu melihat kepada pengamalan umat Islam dengan mengikut apa yang telah dijelaskan oleh para Ulama Fiqh sepanjang zaman. 

Perbincangan ini juga menunjukkan bahawa betapa pentingnya pengajian ilmu secara bersanad agar seseorang dapat memahami kefahaman yang sahih terhadap hadith-hadith RasuluLlah SAW supaya amalannya berada di atas pengertian “Sunnah”. 

Demikian adalah kerana praktik amalan yang dilakukan oleh Umat Islam adalah merupakan tasalsul iaitu berantaian dari umat Islam yang awal, seseorang yang hanya ingin mengamalkan hukum-hakam Islam  dengan hanya berpandukan kepada teks al-Qur’an dan hadith semata-mata akan menatijahkan kepincangan dan kecelaruan dalam amalannya.

Oleh kerana itu, Sayyidina Ibnu Umar (ra) berkata:

العِلْمُ دِيْنٌ وَالصَّلَاةُ دِيْنٌ، فَانْظُرُوا عَمَّنْ تَأْخُذُونَ هَذَا العِلْمَ وَكَيْفَ تُصَلُّونَ هَذِهِ الصَّلّاةَ فَإِنَّكُمْ تُسْأَلُونَ يَوْمَ القِيَامَة

"Ilmu itu agama dan solat itu adalah agama. Maka hendaklah kalian perhatikan daripada siapa kalian mengambil ilmu dan solat kalian kerana sesungguhnya kalian akan ditanya pada Hari Qiamat."
(Riwayat al-Daylami)

Athar Sayyidina Ibnu Umar ini membuktikan bahawa kepentingan sanad bukan sahaja terletak kepada jalan riwayat semata-mata, akan tetapi juga merangkumi jalan pengamalan dan kefahaman.

Imam AbduLlah bin Wahb (w.197H/813M) pernah berkata, “Aku telah terlalu banyak menghimpunkan hadith-hadith maka ia telah membingungkanku, aku sentiasa menyangka bahawa setiap apa yang telah datang dari Nabi Muhammad SAW maka boleh beramal dengannya, maka aku bentangkannya kepada Imam Malik bin Anas dan Imam al-Layth, maka mereka berdua berkata: Ambil (hadith) yang ini dan tinggalkan yang ini”. Imam Malik dan Imam Layth adalah antara pakar Fiqh pada zaman tersebut. 

Imam AbduLlah bin Wahb juga berkata, “Setiap pakar hadith yang tidak berguru kepada Ulama Fiqh, nescaya dia akan tersesat. Dan jika Allah tidak menyelamatkanku menerusi Imam Malik dan Imam Layth, nescaya aku pasti tersesat” (kullu sāhib hadith laysa lahu imām fi al-fiqh fa huwa ḍāllun wa law lā anna Allah anqadhanā bi Mālik wa al-Layth laḍalalna).

(Ruj: Tartib al-Madārik li al-Qādi ‘Iyad, j.1,ms.247, Bāb Ashāb Malik dan al-Jāmi’ fi al-Sunan li Ibni Abi Zayd, ms.119)
